nodes.name: Numerators
nodes.statement_short: Numerators agree.
nodes.statement:
For the numerators, we use that
\begin{align*}
&Z_j-\Pi_{ i_1,\ldots, i_{k-1}} (Z_j)-x\,(Z_{i_k}-\Pi_{ i_1,\ldots, i_{k-1}} (Z_{i_k}))\\
&=Z_j-\Pi_{ i_1,\ldots, i_{k-1}} (Z_j)-x Z_{i_k}+ x \Pi_{ i_1,\ldots, i_{k-1}} (Z_{i_k})\\
&=Z_j-(Z_{i_1}\cdots Z_{i_k})
\left[\begin{array}{c}M^{-1}\big(R_j-xR_{i_k}\big) \\ x\end{array}\right]\\
&=Z_j-\Pi_{ i_1,\ldots, i_{k}} (Z_j)\,.
\end{align*}
using~\eqref{eq:Schur1}.

nodes.name: Proof of exact FDR control in orthogonal design
nodes.statement_short: Show the p-values are WPRDS: after a change of variables, build a Knothe-Rosenblatt transport map that pushes conditional laws upward coordinate-wise.
nodes.statement:
We rely on the {\bf Weak Positive Regression Dependency (WPRDS) property} to prove the result, one may consult~\cite[Page 173]{giraud2014introduction} for instance. We say that a function~$g:[0,1]^K\to \mathds{R}^+$ is {\it nondecreasing} if for any~$p,q\in[0,1]^K$ such that~$p_k\geq q_k$ for every~$k=1,\ldots, K$, we have~$g(p)\geq g(q)$. We say that a Borel set~$\Gamma\in[0,1]^K$ is {\it nondecreasing} if~$g=\mathds 1_\Gamma$ is nondecreasing. In other words  if~$y \in \gamma$ and if~$z\geq0$, then~$y+z \in \gamma$. We say that the~$p$-values~$(\,\widehat p_1=\widehat\alpha_{0,1,K+1},\ldots,\widehat p_K=\widehat\alpha_{K-1,K,K+1})$ satisfy the WPRDS property if for any nondecreasing set~$\Gamma$ 
 and for all~$k^0\in I_0$, the function 
\[
u\mapsto \mathds{P}_{\mu^0}\big[(\,\widehat p_1,\ldots,\widehat p_K)\in\Gamma\big|\widehat p_{k^0}\leq u\big]\text{ is nondecreasing}
\]
where~$\mu^0=\beta^0$ in our  orthogonal design case, and we recall that
\[
I_0=\big\{k\in[K]\ :\ \mathds H_{0,k}\text{ is true}\big\}\,.
\] 
To prove Theorem \ref{thm:independentTest}, note that it is sufficient~\cite[Chapter~8]{giraud2014introduction} to prove that 
\begin{equation} u\mapsto \overline{\mathds{P}}\big[(\,\widehat p_1,\ldots,\widehat p_K)\in\Gamma\big|\widehat p_{k^0}\leq u\big]\text{ is nondecreasing}
\end{equation}
where~$\overline{\mathds{E}},\overline{\operatorname{\mathds{P}}}$ will denote that expectations and probabilities are conditional on~$\{\overline \imath_1,\ldots, \overline \imath_K,\lambda_{K+1}\}$ and under the hypothesis that~$\mu^0=X^\top X\beta^0$. Note that one can integrate in~$\lambda_{K+1}$ to get the statement of Theorem \ref{thm:independentTest}.

\medskip

\noindent
 {$\circ$ \bf Step 1: }We start by giving the joint law of the LARS knots under the alternative in the orthogonal design case. Lemma~\ref{z:l:1} and~\eqref{zazcosh} show that, conditional on~$\{\overline \imath_1,\ldots, \overline \imath_K,\lambda_{K+1}\}$,~$(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_K)$ is distributed on the set~$\lambda_1\geq \lambda_2\geq \cdots\geq \lambda_K\geq \lambda_{K+1}$ and it has a coordinate-wise nondecreasing density. 
 
 Now we can assume without loss of generality  that~$\sigma^2 =1$, in addition because of orthogonality 
~$\rho_k^2=1$ implying that~$F_k=\Phi(\lambda_k)$~$\mathcal{P}_{i,j}=\Phi_i\circ\Phi_j^{-1}=\mathrm{Id}$.  We deduce that, conditional on~$\{\overline \imath_1,\ldots, \overline \imath_K,F_{K+1}\}$,~$(F_1,\ldots,F_K)$ is distributed on the set
\[
\big\{
(f_1,\ldots,f_K)\in\mathds{R}^K\ :\ 
1\geq f_1\geq f_2\geq \cdots\geq f_K\geq F_{K+1})
\big\}\,,
\]
it has an {\bf explicit density} given by~\eqref{zazcosh}, and we denote it by~$h_{\mu^0}$. By the change of variables~$G_k:=\frac{ F_k-F_{K+1}}{ F_{k-1}-F_{K+1}}$ one  obtains that the distribution of~$(G_1,\ldots,G_K)$ is supported on~$[0,1]^K$. More precisely, define
\begin{align*}
\psi(f_1,\ldots,f_K)& :=(g_1,\ldots,g_K)   := (\frac{ f_1-F_{K+1}}{1-F_{K+1}},\ldots,\frac{ f_K-F_{K+1}}{f_{K-1}-F_{K+1}}) \\
\psi^{-1}(g_1,\ldots,g_K)&:=\Big((1-F_{K+1})g_1+F_{K+1},\ldots,(1-F_{K+1})g_1g_2\ldots g_K+F_{K+1}\Big),
\end{align*}
whose inverse Jacobian determinant is 
\[
\det\Big[\frac{\partial \psi}{\partial f_1} \cdots\frac{\partial \psi}{\partial f_K}\Big]^{-1}=\prod_{k=1}^K(f_{k-1}-F_{K+1})=(1-F_{K+1})^K\prod_{k=1}^{K}g_k^{K-k}\,.
\] 
We deduce that the density  of~$(G_1,\ldots,G_K)|\{\overline \imath_1,\ldots,\overline \imath_K,F_{K+1}\}$  at point~$g$ with respect to Lebesgue measure is 
\begin{align} \mathbf{p}(g):=
\mathrm{(const)}\mathds 1_{g\in(0,1)^K}\prod_{k=1}^{K}g_k^{K-k}&\cosh\big[{\mu^0_{\overline\imath_k}}((1-F_{K+1})\prod_{\ell=1}^kg_\ell+F_{K+1})\big]\,,
\end{align}
where we have used~\eqref{zazcosh}. From~\eqref{zaza5} and~\eqref{eq:BetaF}, one has 
\begin{equation} \widehat p_k =1-\boldsymbol{F}_{\beta(1,K-k+1)} \bigg( \frac{ F_k-F_{K+1}}{ F_{k-1}-F_{K+1}} \bigg)
=1-\boldsymbol{F}_{\beta(1,K-k+1)}(G_k)
\end{equation}
 where~$\boldsymbol{F}_\beta$ is the cumulative distribution  of the Beta distribution in reference. We deduce that for any~$v\in(0,1)$ and for any~$\ell\in[K]$, 
\begin{align*}













\widehat p_k &= v
\Leftrightarrow
(G_1,\ldots,G_K)\in 
{[0,1]^K\cap\{\boldsymbol{F}_{\beta(1,K-k+1)}^{-1}(1-v)= G_k\}
}

\,,
\end{align*}
so that 
\begin{equation} \overline{\mathds{P}}\big[(\,\widehat p_1,\ldots,\widehat p_K)\in\Gamma\big|\widehat p_{k^0}\leq u\big]=\overline{\mathds{P}}\big[(G_1,\ldots,G_K)\in\overline\Gamma\big|G_{k^0}\geq \boldsymbol{F}_{\beta(1,K-\ell+1)}^{-1}(1-u)\big]\,,
\end{equation}
where~$\overline\Gamma$ can be proved to be a {\bf nonincreasing Borel set} from~\eqref{eq:yoyoFDR}. 


\medskip

\noindent
 {$\circ$ \bf Step 2: }
 Let~$0<x<y<1$ and denote by~$\mu_x$ the following conditional law  
 \[
 \mu_x:=\mathrm{law}\big[(G_1,\ldots,G_K)|\{\overline \imath_1,\ldots,\overline \imath_K,F_{K+1},G_{k^0}\geq x\}\big]\,.
 \] 
 Remark that if there exists a measurable~$T:[0,1]^K\mapsto [0,1]^K$ such that 
 \begin{itemize}
 \item~$T$ is nondecreasing, meaning that for any~$g\in[0,1]^K$,~$T(g)\geq g$;
 \item~$T$ is such that push-forward of~$\mu_x$ by~$T$ gives~$\mu_y$, namely~$T_\#\mu_x=\mu_y$;
 \end{itemize}
then it holds
 \begin{itemize}
 \item~$\mathds 1_{\{T(g)\in\overline\Gamma\}}\leq\mathds 1_{\{g\in\overline\Gamma\}}$;
 \item~$\mathrm{law}\big[T(G)|\{\overline \imath_1,\ldots,\overline \imath_K,F_{K+1},G_{k^0}\geq x\}\big]=\mathrm{law}\big[G|\{\overline \imath_1,\ldots,\overline \imath_K,F_{K+1},G_{k^0}\geq y\}\big]$ where~$G=(G_1,\ldots,G_K)$.
 \end{itemize}
In this case, we deduce that 
\[
\overline{\mathds{P}}\big[G\in\overline\Gamma\big|G_{k^0}\geq x\big]
\geq
\overline{\mathds{P}}\big[T(G)\in\overline\Gamma\big|G_{k^0}\geq x\big]
=
\overline{\mathds{P}}\big[G\in\overline\Gamma\big|G_{k^0}\geq y\big]\,.
\]
 If one can prove that such function~$T$ exists for any~$0<x<y<1$, it proves that 
 \[
 x\mapsto \overline{\mathds{P}}\big[G\in\overline\Gamma\big|G_{k^0}\geq x\big]\text{ is nonincreasing}\,,
 \]
and, in view of~\eqref{yoyo:Fg}, it proves~\eqref{yoyonondecresaing}. Proving that such function~$T$ exists is done in the next step.

\medskip

\noindent
 {$\circ$ \bf Step 3: }
 Let~$0<x<y<1$. Consider the {\bf Knothe-Rosenblatt transport map}~$T$ of~$\mu_x$ toward~$\mu_y$ following the order
 \[
 k^0\to k^0+1\to\cdots\to K\to k^0-1\to k^0-2\to\cdots\to 1\,.
 \]
 It is based on a sequence of conditional quantile transforms defined following the ordering above. Its construction is presented for instance in~\cite[Sec.2.3, P.67]{santambrogio2015optimal} or~\cite[P.20]{villani2008optimal}. The transport~$T$ is defined as follows. Given~$z,z'\in[0,1]^K$ such that~$z'=T(z)$ it holds
 \begin{align*}
 z'_{k^0}&=T^{(k^0)}(z_{k^0});\\
 z'_{k^0+1}&=T^{(k^0+1)}(z_{k^0+1},z'_{k^0});\\
 &\vdots\\
 z'_K&=T^{(K)}(z_K,z'_{K-1},\ldots,z'_{k^0});\\
 z'_{k^0-1}&=T^{(k^0-1)}(z_{k^0-1},z'_K,\ldots,z'_{k^0});\\
 &\vdots\\
 z'_1&=T^{(1)}(z_1,z'_2,\ldots,z'_{k^0-1},z'_K,\ldots,z'_{k^0});
 \end{align*}
where~$T^{(k^0)}, T^{(k^0+1)},\ldots,T^{(K)},T^{(k^0-1)}\ldots,T^{(1)}$ will be build in the sequel, in which we will drop their dependencies in the~$z'_k$'s to ease notations. It remains to prove that 
 \begin{itemize}
 \item~$T$ is nondecreasing, meaning that for any~$g\in[0,1]^K$,~$T(g)\geq g$;
 \item~$T$ is such that push-forward of~$\mu_x$ by~$T$ gives~$\mu_y$, namely~$T_\#\mu_x=\mu_y$;
 \end{itemize}
 to conclude. The last point is a property of the Knothe-Rosenblatt transport map. Proving the first point will be done in the rest of  the proof.
 
 \medskip
 
\noindent
 {$\circ$ \it Step 3.1: } We start by the first transport map~$T^{(k^0)}:[0,1]\mapsto[0,1]$. Denote~$\mu_x^{(k^0)}$ the following conditional law  
 \[
 \mu_x^{(k^0)}:=\mathrm{law}\big[G_{k^0}|\{\overline \imath_1,\ldots,\overline \imath_K,F_{K+1},G_{k^0}\geq x\}\big]\,,
 \]
 and~$\mathds{F}_x^{(k^0)}$ its cdf. Note that the Knothe-Rosenblatt construction gives~$T^{(k^0)}=(\mathds{F}_y^{(k^0)})^{-1}\circ\mathds{F}_x^{(k^0)}$. We would like to prove that~$T^{(k^0)}(t)\geq t$ for all~$z\in(0,1)$. This is equivalent to prove that it holds~$ \mathds{F}_x^{(k^0)}\geq \mathds{F}_y^{(k^0)}$. For~$t\leq y$,~$\mathds{F}_y^{(k^0)}(t)=0$ and it implies that~$ \mathds{F}_x^{(k^0)}(t)\geq \mathds{F}_y^{(k^0)}(t)$. Let~$t>y$, using the conditional density~$\mathbf{p}$ defined in~\eqref{eq:density}, note that
 
 \begin{align*}
 \mathds{F}_x^{(k^0)}(t)\geq \mathds{F}_y^{(k^0)}(t)\quad&\Leftrightarrow\quad 
 \frac  {\int_x^t\mathbf{p}}  {\int_x^1\mathbf{p}}    \geq 
 \frac  {\int_y^t\mathbf{p}}  {\int_y^1\mathbf{p}} \\
 &\Leftrightarrow\quad \int_x^t \int_y^1 \mathbf{p}\otimes\mathbf{p}
 
 \geq \int_y^t   \int_x^1\mathbf{p}\otimes\mathbf{p},
 \end{align*}
where, for example
\[
\int_x^t \mbox{ means the integral over the  hyper rectangle }  [x,t]
:=\Big\{(g_1,\ldots,g_K)\in[0,1]^K\ :\!\ x\leq g_{k^0}\leq t\Big\}.
\]
A simple calculation (see also Figure~\ref{fig:yoyo}) gives that
\[
\int_x^t \int_y^1 \mathbf{p}\otimes\mathbf{p} = \int_y^t   \int_x^1\mathbf{p}\otimes\mathbf{p} +
\int_{[x,y] \times [t,1]}
\mathbf{p}\otimes\mathbf{p}\,,
\]
and it proves that~$ \mathds{F}_x^{(k^0)}\geq \mathds{F}_y^{(k^0)}$.

\begin{figure}
\includegraphics[width=0.4\textwidth]{y1}
\caption{Note that, by symmetry  the two boxed regions  have same~$ \mathbf{p}\otimes\mathbf{p}$ measure. The blue region is~$[x,t]\times [y,1]~$, its measure is the measure of the red region (namely~$cD_y(t)\times \mathcal{D}_x(1)$) more the bluest upper left corner (namely~$ [x,y]\times[t,1]$). } \end{figure}
 
 \medskip
 
 \noindent
 {$\circ$ \it Step 3.2: } We continue with the second transport map in Knothe-Rosenblatt construction. Let~$z_{k^0}\in(x,1)$ and denote~$\mu_{z_{k^0}}^{(k^0+1)}$ the following conditional law  
 \[
 \mu_{z_{k^0}}^{(k^0+1)}:=\mathrm{law}\big[G_{k^0+1}|\{\overline \imath_1,\ldots,\overline \imath_K,F_{K+1}, G_{k^0}=z_{k^0}\}\big]\,,
 \]
 and~$\mathds{F}_{z_{k^0}}^{(k^0+1)}$ its cdf. Let~$z'_{k^0}:=T^{(k^0)}(z'_{k^0})$ and denote~$\mu_{z'_{k^0}}^{(k^0+1)}$ the following conditional law  
 \[
 \mu_{z'_{k^0}}^{(k^0+1)}:=\mathrm{law}\big[G_{k^0+1}|\{\overline \imath_1,\ldots,\overline \imath_K,F_{K+1}, G_{k^0}=z'_{k^0}\}\big]\,,
 \]
 and~$\mathds{F}_{z'_{k^0}}^{(k^0+1)}$ its cdf. Note that~$x<z_{k^0}\leq z'_{k^0}=T^{(k^0)}(z_{k^0})\leq 1$. Again, we would like to prove that~$\mathds{F}_{z_{k^0}}^{(k^0+1)}\geq \mathds{F}_{z'_{k^0}}^{(k^0+1)}$ which implies that the transport map~$T^{(k^0+1)}:=\big(\mathds{F}_{z'_{k^0}}^{(k^0+1)}\big)^{-1}\circ \mathds{F}_{z_{k^0}}^{(k^0+1)}$ satisfies~$T^{(k^0+1)}(u)\geq u$ for all~$u\in(0,1)$.
 
 Recall that the conditional density~$\mathbf{p}$ of~$G|\{\overline \imath_1,\ldots,\overline \imath_K,F_{K+1}\}$ is given by~\eqref{eq:density} and recall that~$k^0\in I_0$. Observe that~$\mu^0_{k^0}=0$, so that the conditional density of~$G|\{\overline \imath_1,\ldots,\overline \imath_K,F_{K+1}, G_{k^0}=\mathbf{z}\}$ is
 \begin{align}
 \mathrm{(const)}\,\mathds 1_{g\in(0,1)^K}\mathds 1_{g_{k^0}=\mathbf{z}}&\prod_{k< k^0}g_k^{K-k}\cosh\big[{\mu^0_{\overline\imath_k}}((1-F_{K+1})\prod_{\ell=1}^kg_\ell+F_{K+1})\big] \\&\times \prod_{k> k^0}g_k^{K-k}\cosh\big[{\mu^0_{\overline\imath_k}}((1-F_{K+1})\,\,\mathbf{z}\!\!\prod_{1\leq \ell\neq k^0\leq k}\!\!g_\ell+F_{K+1})\big]\,.\notag
 \end{align}
 Set~$\tau:=z'_{k^0}/z_{k^0}\geq 1$ and~$G'_{k^0+1}=\tau G_{k^0+1}$ so that 
 \[
 z_{k^0} G_{k^0+1}=z'_{k^0}G'_{k^0+1}\,.
 \]
 Denote~$G':=(G_1,\ldots,G_{k^0-1},G'_{k^0+1},G_{k^0+2},\ldots,G_K)\in(0,1)^{k^0-1}\times(0,\tau)\times(0,1)^{K-k^0-1}$ and note that the conditional density of~$G'|\{\overline \imath_1,\ldots,\overline \imath_K,F_{K+1}, G_{k^0}=\tau \mathbf{z}\}$ is
 \begin{align*}
 \mathrm{(const)}\,\mathds 1_{g\in(0,1)^{k^0-1}\times(0,\tau)\times(0,1)^{K-k^0-1}}
 &\prod_{k< k^0}g_k^{K-k}\cosh\big[{\mu^0_{\overline\imath_k}}((1-F_{K+1})\prod_{\ell=1}^kg_\ell+F_{K+1})\big]
 \\&\times \prod_{k> k^0}g_k^{K-k}\cosh\big[{\mu^0_{\overline\imath_k}}((1-F_{K+1})\,\,\mathbf{z}\!\!\prod_{1\leq \ell\neq k^0\leq k}\!\!g_\ell+F_{K+1})\big]\,,
 \end{align*}
 which, up to some normalising constant, is the same as~\eqref{yoyoz1} up to the following change of support
 \[
 \mathds 1_{g\in(0,1)^K}\leftrightarrow \mathds 1_{g'\in(0,1)^{k^0-1}\times(0,\tau)\times(0,1)^{K-k^0-1}}\,.
 \]
 By an abuse of notation, we denote by~$\mathbf{p}$ this function, namely
 \begin{align*}
\mathbf{p}(g)=
 &\prod_{k< k^0}g_k^{K-k}\cosh\big[{\mu^0_{\overline\imath_k}}((1-F_{K+1})\prod_{\ell=1}^kg_\ell+F_{K+1})\big]
 \\&\times \prod_{k> k^0}g_k^{K-k}\cosh\big[{\mu^0_{\overline\imath_k}}((1-F_{K+1})\,\,\mathbf{z}\!\!\prod_{1\leq \ell\neq k^0\leq k}\!\!g_\ell+F_{K+1})\big]\,.
 \end{align*}
We deduce that
\begin{align}
 \mathds{F}_{z_{k^0}}^{(k^0+1)}(t)\geq \mathds{F}_{z'_{k^0}}^{(k^0+1)}(t)\quad
 &\Leftrightarrow\quad \overline{\mathds{P}}(G_{k^0+1}\leq t|G_{k^0}=z_{k^0})\geq
 \overline{\mathds{P}}(G_{k^0+1}\leq t|G_{k^0}=z'_{k^0})\notag\\
 &\Leftrightarrow\quad \overline{\mathds{P}}(G_{k^0+1}\leq t|G_{k^0}=z_{k^0})\geq
 \overline{\mathds{P}}(G'_{k^0+1}\leq \tau t|G_{k^0}=\tau z_{k^0})\notag\\
 &\Leftrightarrow\quad \frac{\int_{\mathcal{D}(t)}\mathbf{p}}{\int_{\mathcal{D}(1)}\mathbf{p}} \geq \frac{\int_{\mathcal{D}(\tau t)}\mathbf{p}}{\int_{\mathcal{D}(\tau)}\mathbf{p}}\notag\\
&\Leftrightarrow\quad \int_{\mathcal{D}(t)\times\mathcal{D}(\tau) }\mathbf{p}\otimes\mathbf{p}\geq\int_{\mathcal{D}(\tau t)\times \mathcal{D}(1)}\mathbf{p}\otimes\mathbf{p}\,, \end{align}
where
\[
 \mathcal{D}(s):=\Big\{(g_1,\ldots,g_{k^0-1},g_{k^0+1}\ldots,g_K)\in(0,1)^{K-1}\ :\ 0< g_{k^0+1}\leq s\Big\}\,.
\]
\begin{figure}
\includegraphics[width=0.4\textwidth]{y2}
\caption{The two boxed rectangles have Lebesgue measure, namely~$\tau t$. The~$\mathbf{p}\otimes\mathbf{p}$  measure of the grey box is greater than the~$\mathbf{p}\otimes\mathbf{p}$ measure of the white box. } \end{figure}

We now present an inequality on the  to conclude. Observe that we are integrating on domains depicted in Figure~\ref{fig:yoyo2}. The two boxes have same area for the uniform measure and we would like to compare their respective measure for the~$\mathbf{p}\otimes\mathbf{p}$ measure. We start by the next lemma whose proof is omitted. 
\begin{lemma} Let~$a,b\geq0$. The function 
\[
z\mapsto\cosh(a\, z+b)\times \cosh(a / z+b)
\]
is non-decreasing on the domain~$[1,\infty)$.
\end{lemma}

\noindent
Now, let~$(g_1,\ldots,g_{k^0-1},g_{k^0+2}\ldots,g_K)\in(0,1)^{K-1}$ be fixed in the integrals~\eqref{eq:yoyo123}. We are the looking at the weights of the domains~$(h_1,h_2)\in(0,t)\times (0,\tau)$ and~$(h_3,h_4)\in(0,\tau t)\times (0,1)$ for the weight function~$w$ given by
\begin{align*}
w(h_1,h_2)=&\mathrm{C}_1h_1^{K-k^0-1}\cosh\big[{\mu^0_{\overline\imath_k}}((1-F_{K+1})\,\,z_{k^0}\!\!\prod_{1\leq \ell <k^0}\!\!g_\ell\times h_1+F_{K+1})\big]\\
&\times \prod_{k> k^0+1}\cosh\big[{\mu^0_{\overline\imath_k}}((1-F_{K+1})\,\,z_{k^0}\!\!\prod_{1\leq \ell\neq k^0,k^0+1\leq k}\!\!g_\ell\times h_1+F_{K+1})\big]\\
&\times h_2^{K-k^0-1}\cosh\big[{\mu^0_{\overline\imath_k}}((1-F_{K+1})\,\,z_{k^0}\!\!\prod_{1\leq \ell <k^0}\!\!g_\ell\times h_2+F_{K+1})\big]\\
&\times \prod_{k> k^0+1}\cosh\big[{\mu^0_{\overline\imath_k}}((1-F_{K+1})\,\,z_{k^0}\!\!\prod_{1\leq \ell\neq k^0,k^0+1\leq k}\!\!g_\ell\times h_2+F_{K+1})\big]\,,
 \end{align*}
 where the constant~$\mathrm{C}_1$ depends on~$(g_1,\ldots,g_{k^0-1},g_{k^0+2}\ldots,g_K)\in(0,1)^{K-1}$. By the change of variables~$h'_1=h_3/t$ and~$h'_2=t h_4$, the right hand term of~\eqref{eq:yoyo123} is given by the integration on the domain~$(h'_1,h'_2)\in(0,t)\times (0,\tau)$ of the weight function~$w'$ given by
\begin{align*}
w'(h_1',h_2')=
 &\mathrm{C}_1{h'_1}^{K-k^0-1}\cosh\big[{\mu^0_{\overline\imath_k}}((1-F_{K+1})\,\,z_{k^0}\!\!\prod_{1\leq \ell <k^0}\!\!g_\ell\times t\times h'_1+F_{K+1})\big]\\
&\times \prod_{k> k^0+1}\cosh\big[{\mu^0_{\overline\imath_k}}((1-F_{K+1})\,\,z_{k^0}\!\!\prod_{1\leq \ell\neq k^0,k^0+1\leq k}\!\!g_\ell\times t\times h'_1+F_{K+1})\big]\\
 &\times {h'_2}^{K-k^0-1}\cosh\big[{\mu^0_{\overline\imath_k}}((1-F_{K+1})\,\,z_{k^0}\!\!\prod_{1\leq \ell <k^0}\!\!g_\ell\times h'_2/t+F_{K+1})\big]\\
&\times \prod_{k> k^0+1}\cosh\big[{\mu^0_{\overline\imath_k}}((1-F_{K+1})\,\,z_{k^0}\!\!\prod_{1\leq \ell\neq k^0,k^0+1\leq k}\!\!g_\ell\times h'_2/t+F_{K+1})\big]\,.
 \end{align*}
Now, invoke Lemma~\ref{lem:coshyoyo} with 
\begin{align*}
a&={\mu^0_{\overline\imath_k}}(1-F_{K+1})\,\,z_{k^0}\!\!\prod_{1\leq \ell <k^0}\!\!g_\ell\times  h\\
b&={\mu^0_{\overline\imath_k}}F_{K+1}\\
z&=t\geq 1\,,
\end{align*}
where~$h=h_1$ or~$h_2$, to get that~$w'\geq w$ and so 
\[
\int_{\mathcal{D}(t)\times\mathcal{D}(\tau) }\mathbf{p}\otimes\mathbf{p}\geq\int_{\mathcal{D}(\tau t)\times \mathcal{D}(1)}\mathbf{p}\otimes\mathbf{p}\,,
\]
which concludes this part of the proof.


 \medskip
 
 \noindent
 {$\circ$ \it Step 3.3: } We continue by induction with the other transport maps in Knothe-Rosenblatt's construction. Assume that we have built~$z':=(z'_{k},\ldots,z'_{k^0})$ and~$z:=(z_{k},\ldots,z_{k^0})$ for some~$k>k^0$. Denote~$\mu_{z}^{(k+1)}$ the following conditional law  
 \[
 \mu_{z}^{(k+1)}:=\mathrm{law}\big[G_{k+1}|\{\overline \imath_1,\ldots,\overline \imath_K,F_{K+1}, \underbrace{G_{k}=z_{k},\ldots, G_{k^0}=z_{k^0}}_{\mathrm{denoted\ }G^{[k,k^0]}=z}\}\big]\,,
 \]
 and~$\mathds{F}_{z}^{(k+1)}$ its cdf. Denote~$\mu_{z'}^{(k+1)}$ the following conditional law  
 \[
 \mu_{z'}^{(k+1)}:=\mathrm{law}\big[G_{k+1}|\{\overline \imath_1,\ldots,\overline \imath_K,F_{K+1}, \underbrace{G_{k}=z'_{k},\ldots, G_{k^0}=z'_{k^0}}_{G^{[k,k^0]}=z'}\}\big]\,,
 \]
 and~$\mathds{F}_{z'}^{(k+1)}$ its cdf. Note that~$z\leq z'=T^{(k)}(z)\leq 1$. Again, we would prove that~$\mathds{F}_{z}^{(k+1)}\geq \mathds{F}_{z'}^{(k+1)}$ which implies that the transport map~$T^{(k+1)}:=\big(\mathds{F}_{z'}^{(k+1)}\big)^{-1}\circ \mathds{F}_{z}^{(k+1)}$ satisfies~$T^{(k+1)}(u)\geq u$ for all~$u\in(0,1)$.
 
 For~$\mathbf{z}\in(0,1)^{k-k^0}\times(x,1)$, the conditional density of~$G|\{\overline \imath_1,\ldots,\overline \imath_K,F_{K+1}, G^{[k,k^0]}=\mathbf{z}\}$ is
 \begin{align}
 \mathrm{(const)}\,\mathds 1_{g\in(0,1)^K}&\mathds 1_{g^{[k,k^0]}=\mathbf{z}}
 \prod_{m< k^0}g_m^{K-m}\cosh\big[{\mu^0_{\overline\imath_m}}((1-F_{K+1})\prod_{\ell=1}^mg_\ell+F_{K+1})\big]\notag]\\
 &\times \prod_{k^0\leq m\leq k}\mathbf{z}_m^{K-m}\cosh\big[{\mu^0_{\overline\imath_m}}((1-F_{K+1})\prod_{1\leq \ell<k^0}\!\!g_\ell\,\,\prod_{n=k^0}^m\mathbf{z}_n+F_{K+1})\big]\notag\\
&\times \prod_{k<m}g_m^{K-m}\cosh\big[{\mu^0_{\overline\imath_m}}((1-F_{K+1})\prod_{1\leq \ell<k^0}\!\!g_\ell\,\,\prod_{n=k^0}^k\mathbf{z}_n\prod_{k< \ell\leq m}\!\!g_\ell+F_{K+1})\big]\,.\notag
 \end{align}
Set~$\tau:=\prod_{n=k^0}^kz'_n/\prod_{n=k^0}^kz_n\geq 1$ and~$G'_{k}=\tau G_{k^0+1}$ so that 
 \[
\Big[\prod_{n=k^0}^kz'_n\Big] G_{k+1}=\Big[\prod_{n=k^0}^kz_n\Big] G'_{k+1}\,.
 \]
Then the proof follows the same idea as in {\it Step 3.2} and we will not detail it here.
 \medskip
 
 \noindent
 {$\circ$ \it Step 3.4: } This is the last step of the proof. Assume that we have built~$z':=(z'_{K},\ldots,z'_{k^0})$ and~$z:=(z_{K},\ldots,z_{k^0})$. Denote~$\mu_{z}^{(k^0-1)}$ the following conditional law  
 \[
 \mu_{z}^{(k^0-1)}:=\mathrm{law}\big[G_{k^0-1}|\{\overline \imath_1,\ldots,\overline \imath_K,F_{K+1}, G^{[K,k^0]}=z\}\big]\,,
 \]
 and~$\mathds{F}_{z}^{(k^0-1)}$ its cdf. Denote~$\mu_{z'}^{(k^0-1)}$ the following conditional law  
 \[
 \mu_{z'}^{(k^0-1)}:=\mathrm{law}\big[G_{k^0-1}|\{\overline \imath_1,\ldots,\overline \imath_K,F_{K+1}, G^{[K,k^0]}=z'\}\big]\,,
 \]
 and~$\mathds{F}_{z'}^{(k^01)}$ its cdf. Note that~$z\leq z'=T^{(K)}(z)\leq 1$. Again, we would prove that~$\mathds{F}_{z}^{(k^0-1)}\geq \mathds{F}_{z'}^{(k^0-1)}$ which implies that the transport map~$T^{(k^0-1)}:=\big(\mathds{F}_{z'}^{(k^0-1)}\big)^{-1}\circ \mathds{F}_{z}^{(k^0-1)}$ satisfies~$T^{(k^0-1)}(u)\geq u$ for all~$u\in(0,1)$.

For~$\mathbf{z}\in(0,1)^{K-k^0}\times(x,1)$, the conditional density of~$G|\{\overline \imath_1,\ldots,\overline \imath_K,F_{K+1}, G^{[K,k^0]}=\mathbf{z}\}$ is
 \begin{align}
 \mathrm{(const)}\,\mathds 1_{g\in(0,1)^K}&\mathds 1_{g^{[K,k^0]}=\mathbf{z}}
 \prod_{m< k^0}g_m^{K-m}\cosh\big[{\mu^0_{\overline\imath_m}}((1-F_{K+1})\prod_{\ell=1}^mg_\ell+F_{K+1})\big]\notag\\
 &\times \prod_{k^0\leq m\leq K}\mathbf{z}_m^{K-m}\cosh\big[{\mu^0_{\overline\imath_m}}((1-F_{K+1})\prod_{1\leq \ell<k^0}\!\!g_\ell\,\,\prod_{n=k^0}^m\mathbf{z}_n+F_{K+1})\big]\,.\notag
 \end{align}

\noindent
Now, let~$(g_1,\ldots,g_{k^0-2})\in(0,1)^{k^0-2}$ be fixed and denote by
 \begin{align}
\forall g\in(0,1),\quad
w_{z}(g):=&g^{K-k^0+1}\cosh\big[{\mu^0_{\overline\imath_{k^0-1}}}((1-F_{K+1})\prod_{\ell=1}^{k^0-2}g_\ell\times g+F_{K+1})\big]\notag\\
 &\times \prod_{k^0\leq m\leq K}\mathbf{z}_m^{K-m}\cosh\big[{\mu^0_{\overline\imath_m}}((1-F_{K+1})\prod_{n=k^0}^m\mathbf{z}_n\prod_{\ell=1}^{k^0-2}g_\ell\times g+F_{K+1})\big]\,.\notag
 \end{align}
 and, substituting~$z$ by~$z'$, define~$w_{z'}$ as well. Let~$t\in(0,1)$. Following the idea of  {\it Step 3.2}, one can check that it is sufficient to prove that
 \[
 \int_0^t\Big(\int_0^1w_{z}(g)w_{z'}(g')\mathrm dg'\Big)\mathrm dg
 \geq
  \int_0^1\Big(\int_0^tw_{z}(g)w_{z'}(g')\mathrm dg'\Big)\mathrm dg\,.
 \]
 Substituting 
 \[
  \int_0^t\Big(\int_0^tw_{z}(g)w_{z'}(g')\mathrm dg'\Big)\mathrm dg
 \]
 on both parts, one is reduced to prove that
  \[
 \int_0^t\Big(\int_t^1w_{z}(g)w_{z'}(g')\mathrm dg'\Big)\mathrm dg
 \geq
\int_0^t\Big(\int_t^1w_{z'}(g)w_{z}(g')\mathrm dg'\Big)\mathrm dg\,.
 \]
 Observe that~$g\leq g'$ in the last two integrals. Now, we have this lemma whose proof is omitted. 
 \begin{lemma} Let~$0<a\leq a'$ and~$b>0$. The function 
\[
z\mapsto\frac{\cosh(a\, z+b)}{\cosh(a'z+b)}
\]
is non-increasing on the domain~$(0,\infty)$.
\end{lemma}

\noindent
Let~$g\leq g'$. From Lemma~\ref{lem:coshyoyo2}, we deduce that~$\cosh(a g+b)\cosh(a' g'+b)\geq \cosh(a g'+b)\cosh(a' g+b)$, proving that~$w_{z}(g)w_{z'}(g')\geq w_{z'}(g)w_{z}(g')$. It proves that~$T^{(k^0-1)}(u)\geq u$ for all~$u\in(0,1)$.

We then proceed by induction for~$k^0-1\to k^0-2\to\cdots\to 1$. The proof follows the same line as above, {\it Step 3.4}.

nodes.name: WPRDS reduction
nodes.statement_short: Reduce FDR control to the WPRDS property.
nodes.statement:
We rely on the {\bf Weak Positive Regression Dependency (WPRDS) property} to prove the result, one may consult~\cite[Page 173]{giraud2014introduction} for instance. We say that a function~$g:[0,1]^K\to \mathds{R}^+$ is {\it nondecreasing} if for any~$p,q\in[0,1]^K$ such that~$p_k\geq q_k$ for every~$k=1,\ldots, K$, we have~$g(p)\geq g(q)$. We say that a Borel set~$\Gamma\in[0,1]^K$ is {\it nondecreasing} if~$g=\mathds 1_\Gamma$ is nondecreasing. In other words  if~$y \in \gamma$ and if~$z\geq0$, then~$y+z \in \gamma$. We say that the~$p$-values~$(\,\widehat p_1=\widehat\alpha_{0,1,K+1},\ldots,\widehat p_K=\widehat\alpha_{K-1,K,K+1})$ satisfy the WPRDS property if for any nondecreasing set~$\Gamma$ 
 and for all~$k^0\in I_0$, the function 
\[
u\mapsto \mathds{P}_{\mu^0}\big[(\,\widehat p_1,\ldots,\widehat p_K)\in\Gamma\big|\widehat p_{k^0}\leq u\big]\text{ is nondecreasing}
\]
where~$\mu^0=\beta^0$ in our  orthogonal design case, and we recall that
\[
I_0=\big\{k\in[K]\ :\ \mathds H_{0,k}\text{ is true}\big\}\,.
\] 
To prove Theorem \ref{thm:independentTest}, note that it is sufficient~\cite[Chapter~8]{giraud2014introduction} to prove that 
\begin{equation} u\mapsto \overline{\mathds{P}}\big[(\,\widehat p_1,\ldots,\widehat p_K)\in\Gamma\big|\widehat p_{k^0}\leq u\big]\text{ is nondecreasing}
\end{equation}
where~$\overline{\mathds{E}},\overline{\operatorname{\mathds{P}}}$ will denote that expectations and probabilities are conditional on~$\{\overline \imath_1,\ldots, \overline \imath_K,\lambda_{K+1}\}$ and under the hypothesis that~$\mu^0=X^\top X\beta^0$. Note that one can integrate in~$\lambda_{K+1}$ to get the statement of Theorem \ref{thm:independentTest}.

nodes.name: Rely on WPRDS
nodes.statement_short: BH controls FDR under WPRDS.
nodes.statement: We rely on the {\bf Weak Positive Regression Dependency (WPRDS) property} to prove the result, one may consult~\cite[Page 173]{giraud2014introduction} for instance.

nodes.name: Define WPRDS
nodes.statement_short: Define nondecreasing functions/sets and WPRDS.
nodes.statement:
We say that a function~$g:[0,1]^K\to \mathds{R}^+$ is {\it nondecreasing} if for any~$p,q\in[0,1]^K$ such that~$p_k\geq q_k$ for every~$k=1,\ldots, K$, we have~$g(p)\geq g(q)$. We say that a Borel set~$\Gamma\in[0,1]^K$ is {\it nondecreasing} if~$g=\mathds 1_\Gamma$ is nondecreasing. In other words  if~$y \in \gamma$ and if~$z\geq0$, then~$y+z \in \gamma$. We say that the~$p$-values~$(\,\widehat p_1=\widehat\alpha_{0,1,K+1},\ldots,\widehat p_K=\widehat\alpha_{K-1,K,K+1})$ satisfy the WPRDS property if for any nondecreasing set~$\Gamma$ 
 and for all~$k^0\in I_0$, the function 
\[
u\mapsto \mathds{P}_{\mu^0}\big[(\,\widehat p_1,\ldots,\widehat p_K)\in\Gamma\big|\widehat p_{k^0}\leq u\big]\text{ is nondecreasing}
\]
where~$\mu^0=\beta^0$ in our  orthogonal design case, and we recall that
\[
I_0=\big\{k\in[K]\ :\ \mathds H_{0,k}\text{ is true}\big\}\,.
\]

nodes.name: Sufficient condition
nodes.statement_short: Suffices to prove monotonicity conditionally on the entering sequence and $\lambda_{K+1}$.

nodes.name: Equation (7.11)
nodes.statement: u\mapsto \overline{\mathds{P}}\big[(\,\widehat p_1,\ldots,\widehat p_K)\in\Gamma\big|\widehat p_{k^0}\leq u\big]\text{ is nondecreasing}
nodes.label: yoyonondecresaing

nodes.name: Step 1
nodes.statement_short: Joint law and change of variables to $G$.
nodes.statement:
{$\circ$ \bf Step 1: }We start by giving the joint law of the LARS knots under the alternative in the orthogonal design case. Lemma~\ref{z:l:1} and~\eqref{zazcosh} show that, conditional on~$\{\overline \imath_1,\ldots, \overline \imath_K,\lambda_{K+1}\}$,~$(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_K)$ is distributed on the set~$\lambda_1\geq \lambda_2\geq \cdots\geq \lambda_K\geq \lambda_{K+1}$ and it has a coordinate-wise nondecreasing density. 
 
 Now we can assume without loss of generality  that~$\sigma^2 =1$, in addition because of orthogonality 
~$\rho_k^2=1$ implying that~$F_k=\Phi(\lambda_k)$~$\mathcal{P}_{i,j}=\Phi_i\circ\Phi_j^{-1}=\mathrm{Id}$.  We deduce that, conditional on~$\{\overline \imath_1,\ldots, \overline \imath_K,F_{K+1}\}$,~$(F_1,\ldots,F_K)$ is distributed on the set
\[
\big\{
(f_1,\ldots,f_K)\in\mathds{R}^K\ :\ 
1\geq f_1\geq f_2\geq \cdots\geq f_K\geq F_{K+1})
\big\}\,,
\]
it has an {\bf explicit density} given by~\eqref{zazcosh}, and we denote it by~$h_{\mu^0}$. By the change of variables~$G_k:=\frac{ F_k-F_{K+1}}{ F_{k-1}-F_{K+1}}$ one  obtains that the distribution of~$(G_1,\ldots,G_K)$ is supported on~$[0,1]^K$. More precisely, define
\begin{align*}
\psi(f_1,\ldots,f_K)& :=(g_1,\ldots,g_K)   := (\frac{ f_1-F_{K+1}}{1-F_{K+1}},\ldots,\frac{ f_K-F_{K+1}}{f_{K-1}-F_{K+1}}) \\
\psi^{-1}(g_1,\ldots,g_K)&:=\Big((1-F_{K+1})g_1+F_{K+1},\ldots,(1-F_{K+1})g_1g_2\ldots g_K+F_{K+1}\Big),
\end{align*}
whose inverse Jacobian determinant is 
\[
\det\Big[\frac{\partial \psi}{\partial f_1} \cdots\frac{\partial \psi}{\partial f_K}\Big]^{-1}=\prod_{k=1}^K(f_{k-1}-F_{K+1})=(1-F_{K+1})^K\prod_{k=1}^{K}g_k^{K-k}\,.
\] 
We deduce that the density  of~$(G_1,\ldots,G_K)|\{\overline \imath_1,\ldots,\overline \imath_K,F_{K+1}\}$  at point~$g$ with respect to Lebesgue measure is 
\begin{align} \mathbf{p}(g):=
\mathrm{(const)}\mathds 1_{g\in(0,1)^K}\prod_{k=1}^{K}g_k^{K-k}&\cosh\big[{\mu^0_{\overline\imath_k}}((1-F_{K+1})\prod_{\ell=1}^kg_\ell+F_{K+1})\big]\,,
\end{align}
where we have used~\eqref{zazcosh}. From~\eqref{zaza5} and~\eqref{eq:BetaF}, one has 
\begin{equation} \widehat p_k =1-\boldsymbol{F}_{\beta(1,K-k+1)} \bigg( \frac{ F_k-F_{K+1}}{ F_{k-1}-F_{K+1}} \bigg)
=1-\boldsymbol{F}_{\beta(1,K-k+1)}(G_k)
\end{equation}
 where~$\boldsymbol{F}_\beta$ is the cumulative distribution  of the Beta distribution in reference. We deduce that for any~$v\in(0,1)$ and for any~$\ell\in[K]$, 
\begin{align*}













\widehat p_k &= v
\Leftrightarrow
(G_1,\ldots,G_K)\in 
{[0,1]^K\cap\{\boldsymbol{F}_{\beta(1,K-k+1)}^{-1}(1-v)= G_k\}
}

\,,
\end{align*}
so that 
\begin{equation} \overline{\mathds{P}}\big[(\,\widehat p_1,\ldots,\widehat p_K)\in\Gamma\big|\widehat p_{k^0}\leq u\big]=\overline{\mathds{P}}\big[(G_1,\ldots,G_K)\in\overline\Gamma\big|G_{k^0}\geq \boldsymbol{F}_{\beta(1,K-\ell+1)}^{-1}(1-u)\big]\,,
\end{equation}
where~$\overline\Gamma$ can be proved to be a {\bf nonincreasing Borel set} from~\eqref{eq:yoyoFDR}.

nodes.name: Monotone density
nodes.statement_short: Alternative density is coordinate-wise nondecreasing.
nodes.statement: We start by giving the joint law of the LARS knots under the alternative in the orthogonal design case. Lemma~\ref{z:l:1} and~\eqref{zazcosh} show that, conditional on~$\{\overline \imath_1,\ldots, \overline \imath_K,\lambda_{K+1}\}$,~$(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_K)$ is distributed on the set~$\lambda_1\geq \lambda_2\geq \cdots\geq \lambda_K\geq \lambda_{K+1}$ and it has a coordinate-wise nondecreasing density.

nodes.name: Reduction
nodes.statement_short: WLOG $\sigma=1$; orthogonality makes $\mathcal P_{ij}$ the identity.
nodes.statement:
Now we can assume without loss of generality  that~$\sigma^2 =1$, in addition because of orthogonality 
~$\rho_k^2=1$ implying that~$F_k=\Phi(\lambda_k)$~$\mathcal{P}_{i,j}=\Phi_i\circ\Phi_j^{-1}=\mathrm{Id}$.  We deduce that, conditional on~$\{\overline \imath_1,\ldots, \overline \imath_K,F_{K+1}\}$,~$(F_1,\ldots,F_K)$ is distributed on the set
\[
\big\{
(f_1,\ldots,f_K)\in\mathds{R}^K\ :\ 
1\geq f_1\geq f_2\geq \cdots\geq f_K\geq F_{K+1})
\big\}\,,
\]
it has an {\bf explicit density} given by~\eqref{zazcosh}, and we denote it by~$h_{\mu^0}$.

nodes.name: Change of variables
nodes.statement_short: Change of variables to ratios $G_k$ and their density.
nodes.statement:
By the change of variables~$G_k:=\frac{ F_k-F_{K+1}}{ F_{k-1}-F_{K+1}}$ one  obtains that the distribution of~$(G_1,\ldots,G_K)$ is supported on~$[0,1]^K$. More precisely, define
\begin{align*}
\psi(f_1,\ldots,f_K)& :=(g_1,\ldots,g_K)   := (\frac{ f_1-F_{K+1}}{1-F_{K+1}},\ldots,\frac{ f_K-F_{K+1}}{f_{K-1}-F_{K+1}}) \\
\psi^{-1}(g_1,\ldots,g_K)&:=\Big((1-F_{K+1})g_1+F_{K+1},\ldots,(1-F_{K+1})g_1g_2\ldots g_K+F_{K+1}\Big),
\end{align*}
whose inverse Jacobian determinant is 
\[
\det\Big[\frac{\partial \psi}{\partial f_1} \cdots\frac{\partial \psi}{\partial f_K}\Big]^{-1}=\prod_{k=1}^K(f_{k-1}-F_{K+1})=(1-F_{K+1})^K\prod_{k=1}^{K}g_k^{K-k}\,.
\] 
We deduce that the density  of~$(G_1,\ldots,G_K)|\{\overline \imath_1,\ldots,\overline \imath_K,F_{K+1}\}$  at point~$g$ with respect to Lebesgue measure is 
\begin{align} \mathbf{p}(g):=
\mathrm{(const)}\mathds 1_{g\in(0,1)^K}\prod_{k=1}^{K}g_k^{K-k}&\cosh\big[{\mu^0_{\overline\imath_k}}((1-F_{K+1})\prod_{\ell=1}^kg_\ell+F_{K+1})\big]\,,
\end{align}
where we have used~\eqref{zazcosh}.

nodes.name: Equation (7.12)
nodes.statement:
\mathbf{p}(g):=
\mathrm{(const)}\mathds 1_{g\in(0,1)^K}\prod_{k=1}^{K}g_k^{K-k}&\cosh\big[{\mu^0_{\overline\imath_k}}((1-F_{K+1})\prod_{\ell=1}^kg_\ell+F_{K+1})\big]\,,
nodes.label: eq:density

nodes.name: p-values via G
nodes.statement_short: p-values are monotone functions of $G_k$.

nodes.name: Equation (7.13)
nodes.statement:
\widehat p_k =1-\boldsymbol{F}_{\beta(1,K-k+1)} \bigg( \frac{ F_k-F_{K+1}}{ F_{k-1}-F_{K+1}} \bigg)
=1-\boldsymbol{F}_{\beta(1,K-k+1)}(G_k)
nodes.label: eq:yoyoFDR

nodes.name: Equation (7.14)
nodes.statement: \overline{\mathds{P}}\big[(\,\widehat p_1,\ldots,\widehat p_K)\in\Gamma\big|\widehat p_{k^0}\leq u\big]=\overline{\mathds{P}}\big[(G_1,\ldots,G_K)\in\overline\Gamma\big|G_{k^0}\geq \boldsymbol{F}_{\beta(1,K-\ell+1)}^{-1}(1-u)\big]\,,
nodes.label: yoyo:Fg

nodes.name: Step 2
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to existence of a monotone transport.
nodes.statement:
{$\circ$ \bf Step 2: }
 Let~$0<x<y<1$ and denote by~$\mu_x$ the following conditional law  
 \[
 \mu_x:=\mathrm{law}\big[(G_1,\ldots,G_K)|\{\overline \imath_1,\ldots,\overline \imath_K,F_{K+1},G_{k^0}\geq x\}\big]\,.
 \] 
 Remark that if there exists a measurable~$T:[0,1]^K\mapsto [0,1]^K$ such that 
 \begin{itemize}
 \item~$T$ is nondecreasing, meaning that for any~$g\in[0,1]^K$,~$T(g)\geq g$;
 \item~$T$ is such that push-forward of~$\mu_x$ by~$T$ gives~$\mu_y$, namely~$T_\#\mu_x=\mu_y$;
 \end{itemize}
then it holds
 \begin{itemize}
 \item~$\mathds 1_{\{T(g)\in\overline\Gamma\}}\leq\mathds 1_{\{g\in\overline\Gamma\}}$;
 \item~$\mathrm{law}\big[T(G)|\{\overline \imath_1,\ldots,\overline \imath_K,F_{K+1},G_{k^0}\geq x\}\big]=\mathrm{law}\big[G|\{\overline \imath_1,\ldots,\overline \imath_K,F_{K+1},G_{k^0}\geq y\}\big]$ where~$G=(G_1,\ldots,G_K)$.
 \end{itemize}
In this case, we deduce that 
\[
\overline{\mathds{P}}\big[G\in\overline\Gamma\big|G_{k^0}\geq x\big]
\geq
\overline{\mathds{P}}\big[T(G)\in\overline\Gamma\big|G_{k^0}\geq x\big]
=
\overline{\mathds{P}}\big[G\in\overline\Gamma\big|G_{k^0}\geq y\big]\,.
\]
 If one can prove that such function~$T$ exists for any~$0<x<y<1$, it proves that 
 \[
 x\mapsto \overline{\mathds{P}}\big[G\in\overline\Gamma\big|G_{k^0}\geq x\big]\text{ is nonincreasing}\,,
 \]
and, in view of~\eqref{yoyo:Fg}, it proves~\eqref{yoyonondecresaing}. Proving that such function~$T$ exists is done in the next step.

nodes.name: Define mu_x
nodes.statement_short: Define conditional laws $\mu_x$.
nodes.statement:
Let~$0<x<y<1$ and denote by~$\mu_x$ the following conditional law  
 \[
 \mu_x:=\mathrm{law}\big[(G_1,\ldots,G_K)|\{\overline \imath_1,\ldots,\overline \imath_K,F_{K+1},G_{k^0}\geq x\}\big]\,.
 \]

nodes.name: Transport implies inequality
nodes.statement_short: A nondecreasing transport from $\mu_x$ to $\mu_y$ gives the inequality.

nodes.name: Conclude reduction
nodes.statement_short: Existence gives the WPRDS monotonicity.
nodes.statement:
If one can prove that such function~$T$ exists for any~$0<x<y<1$, it proves that 
 \[
 x\mapsto \overline{\mathds{P}}\big[G\in\overline\Gamma\big|G_{k^0}\geq x\big]\text{ is nonincreasing}\,,
 \]
and, in view of~\eqref{yoyo:Fg}, it proves~\eqref{yoyonondecresaing}. Proving that such function~$T$ exists is done in the next step.

nodes.name: Step 3
nodes.statement_short: Construct the Knothe-Rosenblatt map and show it is nondecreasing.
nodes.statement:
{$\circ$ \bf Step 3: }
 Let~$0<x<y<1$. Consider the {\bf Knothe-Rosenblatt transport map}~$T$ of~$\mu_x$ toward~$\mu_y$ following the order
 \[
 k^0\to k^0+1\to\cdots\to K\to k^0-1\to k^0-2\to\cdots\to 1\,.
 \]
 It is based on a sequence of conditional quantile transforms defined following the ordering above. Its construction is presented for instance in~\cite[Sec.2.3, P.67]{santambrogio2015optimal} or~\cite[P.20]{villani2008optimal}. The transport~$T$ is defined as follows. Given~$z,z'\in[0,1]^K$ such that~$z'=T(z)$ it holds
 \begin{align*}
 z'_{k^0}&=T^{(k^0)}(z_{k^0});\\
 z'_{k^0+1}&=T^{(k^0+1)}(z_{k^0+1},z'_{k^0});\\
 &\vdots\\
 z'_K&=T^{(K)}(z_K,z'_{K-1},\ldots,z'_{k^0});\\
 z'_{k^0-1}&=T^{(k^0-1)}(z_{k^0-1},z'_K,\ldots,z'_{k^0});\\
 &\vdots\\
 z'_1&=T^{(1)}(z_1,z'_2,\ldots,z'_{k^0-1},z'_K,\ldots,z'_{k^0});
 \end{align*}
where~$T^{(k^0)}, T^{(k^0+1)},\ldots,T^{(K)},T^{(k^0-1)}\ldots,T^{(1)}$ will be build in the sequel, in which we will drop their dependencies in the~$z'_k$'s to ease notations. It remains to prove that 
 \begin{itemize}
 \item~$T$ is nondecreasing, meaning that for any~$g\in[0,1]^K$,~$T(g)\geq g$;
 \item~$T$ is such that push-forward of~$\mu_x$ by~$T$ gives~$\mu_y$, namely~$T_\#\mu_x=\mu_y$;
 \end{itemize}
 to conclude. The last point is a property of the Knothe-Rosenblatt transport map. Proving the first point will be done in the rest of  the proof.
 
 \medskip
 
\noindent
 {$\circ$ \it Step 3.1: } We start by the first transport map~$T^{(k^0)}:[0,1]\mapsto[0,1]$. Denote~$\mu_x^{(k^0)}$ the following conditional law  
 \[
 \mu_x^{(k^0)}:=\mathrm{law}\big[G_{k^0}|\{\overline \imath_1,\ldots,\overline \imath_K,F_{K+1},G_{k^0}\geq x\}\big]\,,
 \]
 and~$\mathds{F}_x^{(k^0)}$ its cdf. Note that the Knothe-Rosenblatt construction gives~$T^{(k^0)}=(\mathds{F}_y^{(k^0)})^{-1}\circ\mathds{F}_x^{(k^0)}$. We would like to prove that~$T^{(k^0)}(t)\geq t$ for all~$z\in(0,1)$. This is equivalent to prove that it holds~$ \mathds{F}_x^{(k^0)}\geq \mathds{F}_y^{(k^0)}$. For~$t\leq y$,~$\mathds{F}_y^{(k^0)}(t)=0$ and it implies that~$ \mathds{F}_x^{(k^0)}(t)\geq \mathds{F}_y^{(k^0)}(t)$. Let~$t>y$, using the conditional density~$\mathbf{p}$ defined in~\eqref{eq:density}, note that
 
 \begin{align*}
 \mathds{F}_x^{(k^0)}(t)\geq \mathds{F}_y^{(k^0)}(t)\quad&\Leftrightarrow\quad 
 \frac  {\int_x^t\mathbf{p}}  {\int_x^1\mathbf{p}}    \geq 
 \frac  {\int_y^t\mathbf{p}}  {\int_y^1\mathbf{p}} \\
 &\Leftrightarrow\quad \int_x^t \int_y^1 \mathbf{p}\otimes\mathbf{p}
 
 \geq \int_y^t   \int_x^1\mathbf{p}\otimes\mathbf{p},
 \end{align*}
where, for example
\[
\int_x^t \mbox{ means the integral over the  hyper rectangle }  [x,t]
:=\Big\{(g_1,\ldots,g_K)\in[0,1]^K\ :\!\ x\leq g_{k^0}\leq t\Big\}.
\]
A simple calculation (see also Figure~\ref{fig:yoyo}) gives that
\[
\int_x^t \int_y^1 \mathbf{p}\otimes\mathbf{p} = \int_y^t   \int_x^1\mathbf{p}\otimes\mathbf{p} +
\int_{[x,y] \times [t,1]}
\mathbf{p}\otimes\mathbf{p}\,,
\]
and it proves that~$ \mathds{F}_x^{(k^0)}\geq \mathds{F}_y^{(k^0)}$.

\begin{figure}
\includegraphics[width=0.4\textwidth]{y1}
\caption{Note that, by symmetry  the two boxed regions  have same~$ \mathbf{p}\otimes\mathbf{p}$ measure. The blue region is~$[x,t]\times [y,1]~$, its measure is the measure of the red region (namely~$cD_y(t)\times \mathcal{D}_x(1)$) more the bluest upper left corner (namely~$ [x,y]\times[t,1]$). } \end{figure}
 
 \medskip
 
 \noindent
 {$\circ$ \it Step 3.2: } We continue with the second transport map in Knothe-Rosenblatt construction. Let~$z_{k^0}\in(x,1)$ and denote~$\mu_{z_{k^0}}^{(k^0+1)}$ the following conditional law  
 \[
 \mu_{z_{k^0}}^{(k^0+1)}:=\mathrm{law}\big[G_{k^0+1}|\{\overline \imath_1,\ldots,\overline \imath_K,F_{K+1}, G_{k^0}=z_{k^0}\}\big]\,,
 \]
 and~$\mathds{F}_{z_{k^0}}^{(k^0+1)}$ its cdf. Let~$z'_{k^0}:=T^{(k^0)}(z'_{k^0})$ and denote~$\mu_{z'_{k^0}}^{(k^0+1)}$ the following conditional law  
 \[
 \mu_{z'_{k^0}}^{(k^0+1)}:=\mathrm{law}\big[G_{k^0+1}|\{\overline \imath_1,\ldots,\overline \imath_K,F_{K+1}, G_{k^0}=z'_{k^0}\}\big]\,,
 \]
 and~$\mathds{F}_{z'_{k^0}}^{(k^0+1)}$ its cdf. Note that~$x<z_{k^0}\leq z'_{k^0}=T^{(k^0)}(z_{k^0})\leq 1$. Again, we would like to prove that~$\mathds{F}_{z_{k^0}}^{(k^0+1)}\geq \mathds{F}_{z'_{k^0}}^{(k^0+1)}$ which implies that the transport map~$T^{(k^0+1)}:=\big(\mathds{F}_{z'_{k^0}}^{(k^0+1)}\big)^{-1}\circ \mathds{F}_{z_{k^0}}^{(k^0+1)}$ satisfies~$T^{(k^0+1)}(u)\geq u$ for all~$u\in(0,1)$.
 
 Recall that the conditional density~$\mathbf{p}$ of~$G|\{\overline \imath_1,\ldots,\overline \imath_K,F_{K+1}\}$ is given by~\eqref{eq:density} and recall that~$k^0\in I_0$. Observe that~$\mu^0_{k^0}=0$, so that the conditional density of~$G|\{\overline \imath_1,\ldots,\overline \imath_K,F_{K+1}, G_{k^0}=\mathbf{z}\}$ is
 \begin{align}
 \mathrm{(const)}\,\mathds 1_{g\in(0,1)^K}\mathds 1_{g_{k^0}=\mathbf{z}}&\prod_{k< k^0}g_k^{K-k}\cosh\big[{\mu^0_{\overline\imath_k}}((1-F_{K+1})\prod_{\ell=1}^kg_\ell+F_{K+1})\big] \\&\times \prod_{k> k^0}g_k^{K-k}\cosh\big[{\mu^0_{\overline\imath_k}}((1-F_{K+1})\,\,\mathbf{z}\!\!\prod_{1\leq \ell\neq k^0\leq k}\!\!g_\ell+F_{K+1})\big]\,.\notag
 \end{align}
 Set~$\tau:=z'_{k^0}/z_{k^0}\geq 1$ and~$G'_{k^0+1}=\tau G_{k^0+1}$ so that 
 \[
 z_{k^0} G_{k^0+1}=z'_{k^0}G'_{k^0+1}\,.
 \]
 Denote~$G':=(G_1,\ldots,G_{k^0-1},G'_{k^0+1},G_{k^0+2},\ldots,G_K)\in(0,1)^{k^0-1}\times(0,\tau)\times(0,1)^{K-k^0-1}$ and note that the conditional density of~$G'|\{\overline \imath_1,\ldots,\overline \imath_K,F_{K+1}, G_{k^0}=\tau \mathbf{z}\}$ is
 \begin{align*}
 \mathrm{(const)}\,\mathds 1_{g\in(0,1)^{k^0-1}\times(0,\tau)\times(0,1)^{K-k^0-1}}
 &\prod_{k< k^0}g_k^{K-k}\cosh\big[{\mu^0_{\overline\imath_k}}((1-F_{K+1})\prod_{\ell=1}^kg_\ell+F_{K+1})\big]
 \\&\times \prod_{k> k^0}g_k^{K-k}\cosh\big[{\mu^0_{\overline\imath_k}}((1-F_{K+1})\,\,\mathbf{z}\!\!\prod_{1\leq \ell\neq k^0\leq k}\!\!g_\ell+F_{K+1})\big]\,,
 \end{align*}
 which, up to some normalising constant, is the same as~\eqref{yoyoz1} up to the following change of support
 \[
 \mathds 1_{g\in(0,1)^K}\leftrightarrow \mathds 1_{g'\in(0,1)^{k^0-1}\times(0,\tau)\times(0,1)^{K-k^0-1}}\,.
 \]
 By an abuse of notation, we denote by~$\mathbf{p}$ this function, namely
 \begin{align*}
\mathbf{p}(g)=
 &\prod_{k< k^0}g_k^{K-k}\cosh\big[{\mu^0_{\overline\imath_k}}((1-F_{K+1})\prod_{\ell=1}^kg_\ell+F_{K+1})\big]
 \\&\times \prod_{k> k^0}g_k^{K-k}\cosh\big[{\mu^0_{\overline\imath_k}}((1-F_{K+1})\,\,\mathbf{z}\!\!\prod_{1\leq \ell\neq k^0\leq k}\!\!g_\ell+F_{K+1})\big]\,.
 \end{align*}
We deduce that
\begin{align}
 \mathds{F}_{z_{k^0}}^{(k^0+1)}(t)\geq \mathds{F}_{z'_{k^0}}^{(k^0+1)}(t)\quad
 &\Leftrightarrow\quad \overline{\mathds{P}}(G_{k^0+1}\leq t|G_{k^0}=z_{k^0})\geq
 \overline{\mathds{P}}(G_{k^0+1}\leq t|G_{k^0}=z'_{k^0})\notag\\
 &\Leftrightarrow\quad \overline{\mathds{P}}(G_{k^0+1}\leq t|G_{k^0}=z_{k^0})\geq
 \overline{\mathds{P}}(G'_{k^0+1}\leq \tau t|G_{k^0}=\tau z_{k^0})\notag\\
 &\Leftrightarrow\quad \frac{\int_{\mathcal{D}(t)}\mathbf{p}}{\int_{\mathcal{D}(1)}\mathbf{p}} \geq \frac{\int_{\mathcal{D}(\tau t)}\mathbf{p}}{\int_{\mathcal{D}(\tau)}\mathbf{p}}\notag\\
&\Leftrightarrow\quad \int_{\mathcal{D}(t)\times\mathcal{D}(\tau) }\mathbf{p}\otimes\mathbf{p}\geq\int_{\mathcal{D}(\tau t)\times \mathcal{D}(1)}\mathbf{p}\otimes\mathbf{p}\,, \end{align}
where
\[
 \mathcal{D}(s):=\Big\{(g_1,\ldots,g_{k^0-1},g_{k^0+1}\ldots,g_K)\in(0,1)^{K-1}\ :\ 0< g_{k^0+1}\leq s\Big\}\,.
\]
\begin{figure}
\includegraphics[width=0.4\textwidth]{y2}
\caption{The two boxed rectangles have Lebesgue measure, namely~$\tau t$. The~$\mathbf{p}\otimes\mathbf{p}$  measure of the grey box is greater than the~$\mathbf{p}\otimes\mathbf{p}$ measure of the white box. } \end{figure}

We now present an inequality on the  to conclude. Observe that we are integrating on domains depicted in Figure~\ref{fig:yoyo2}. The two boxes have same area for the uniform measure and we would like to compare their respective measure for the~$\mathbf{p}\otimes\mathbf{p}$ measure. We start by the next lemma whose proof is omitted. 
\begin{lemma} Let~$a,b\geq0$. The function 
\[
z\mapsto\cosh(a\, z+b)\times \cosh(a / z+b)
\]
is non-decreasing on the domain~$[1,\infty)$.
\end{lemma}

\noindent
Now, let~$(g_1,\ldots,g_{k^0-1},g_{k^0+2}\ldots,g_K)\in(0,1)^{K-1}$ be fixed in the integrals~\eqref{eq:yoyo123}. We are the looking at the weights of the domains~$(h_1,h_2)\in(0,t)\times (0,\tau)$ and~$(h_3,h_4)\in(0,\tau t)\times (0,1)$ for the weight function~$w$ given by
\begin{align*}
w(h_1,h_2)=&\mathrm{C}_1h_1^{K-k^0-1}\cosh\big[{\mu^0_{\overline\imath_k}}((1-F_{K+1})\,\,z_{k^0}\!\!\prod_{1\leq \ell <k^0}\!\!g_\ell\times h_1+F_{K+1})\big]\\
&\times \prod_{k> k^0+1}\cosh\big[{\mu^0_{\overline\imath_k}}((1-F_{K+1})\,\,z_{k^0}\!\!\prod_{1\leq \ell\neq k^0,k^0+1\leq k}\!\!g_\ell\times h_1+F_{K+1})\big]\\
&\times h_2^{K-k^0-1}\cosh\big[{\mu^0_{\overline\imath_k}}((1-F_{K+1})\,\,z_{k^0}\!\!\prod_{1\leq \ell <k^0}\!\!g_\ell\times h_2+F_{K+1})\big]\\
&\times \prod_{k> k^0+1}\cosh\big[{\mu^0_{\overline\imath_k}}((1-F_{K+1})\,\,z_{k^0}\!\!\prod_{1\leq \ell\neq k^0,k^0+1\leq k}\!\!g_\ell\times h_2+F_{K+1})\big]\,,
 \end{align*}
 where the constant~$\mathrm{C}_1$ depends on~$(g_1,\ldots,g_{k^0-1},g_{k^0+2}\ldots,g_K)\in(0,1)^{K-1}$. By the change of variables~$h'_1=h_3/t$ and~$h'_2=t h_4$, the right hand term of~\eqref{eq:yoyo123} is given by the integration on the domain~$(h'_1,h'_2)\in(0,t)\times (0,\tau)$ of the weight function~$w'$ given by
\begin{align*}
w'(h_1',h_2')=
 &\mathrm{C}_1{h'_1}^{K-k^0-1}\cosh\big[{\mu^0_{\overline\imath_k}}((1-F_{K+1})\,\,z_{k^0}\!\!\prod_{1\leq \ell <k^0}\!\!g_\ell\times t\times h'_1+F_{K+1})\big]\\
&\times \prod_{k> k^0+1}\cosh\big[{\mu^0_{\overline\imath_k}}((1-F_{K+1})\,\,z_{k^0}\!\!\prod_{1\leq \ell\neq k^0,k^0+1\leq k}\!\!g_\ell\times t\times h'_1+F_{K+1})\big]\\
 &\times {h'_2}^{K-k^0-1}\cosh\big[{\mu^0_{\overline\imath_k}}((1-F_{K+1})\,\,z_{k^0}\!\!\prod_{1\leq \ell <k^0}\!\!g_\ell\times h'_2/t+F_{K+1})\big]\\
&\times \prod_{k> k^0+1}\cosh\big[{\mu^0_{\overline\imath_k}}((1-F_{K+1})\,\,z_{k^0}\!\!\prod_{1\leq \ell\neq k^0,k^0+1\leq k}\!\!g_\ell\times h'_2/t+F_{K+1})\big]\,.
 \end{align*}
Now, invoke Lemma~\ref{lem:coshyoyo} with 
\begin{align*}
a&={\mu^0_{\overline\imath_k}}(1-F_{K+1})\,\,z_{k^0}\!\!\prod_{1\leq \ell <k^0}\!\!g_\ell\times  h\\
b&={\mu^0_{\overline\imath_k}}F_{K+1}\\
z&=t\geq 1\,,
\end{align*}
where~$h=h_1$ or~$h_2$, to get that~$w'\geq w$ and so 
\[
\int_{\mathcal{D}(t)\times\mathcal{D}(\tau) }\mathbf{p}\otimes\mathbf{p}\geq\int_{\mathcal{D}(\tau t)\times \mathcal{D}(1)}\mathbf{p}\otimes\mathbf{p}\,,
\]
which concludes this part of the proof.


 \medskip
 
 \noindent
 {$\circ$ \it Step 3.3: } We continue by induction with the other transport maps in Knothe-Rosenblatt's construction. Assume that we have built~$z':=(z'_{k},\ldots,z'_{k^0})$ and~$z:=(z_{k},\ldots,z_{k^0})$ for some~$k>k^0$. Denote~$\mu_{z}^{(k+1)}$ the following conditional law  
 \[
 \mu_{z}^{(k+1)}:=\mathrm{law}\big[G_{k+1}|\{\overline \imath_1,\ldots,\overline \imath_K,F_{K+1}, \underbrace{G_{k}=z_{k},\ldots, G_{k^0}=z_{k^0}}_{\mathrm{denoted\ }G^{[k,k^0]}=z}\}\big]\,,
 \]
 and~$\mathds{F}_{z}^{(k+1)}$ its cdf. Denote~$\mu_{z'}^{(k+1)}$ the following conditional law  
 \[
 \mu_{z'}^{(k+1)}:=\mathrm{law}\big[G_{k+1}|\{\overline \imath_1,\ldots,\overline \imath_K,F_{K+1}, \underbrace{G_{k}=z'_{k},\ldots, G_{k^0}=z'_{k^0}}_{G^{[k,k^0]}=z'}\}\big]\,,
 \]
 and~$\mathds{F}_{z'}^{(k+1)}$ its cdf. Note that~$z\leq z'=T^{(k)}(z)\leq 1$. Again, we would prove that~$\mathds{F}_{z}^{(k+1)}\geq \mathds{F}_{z'}^{(k+1)}$ which implies that the transport map~$T^{(k+1)}:=\big(\mathds{F}_{z'}^{(k+1)}\big)^{-1}\circ \mathds{F}_{z}^{(k+1)}$ satisfies~$T^{(k+1)}(u)\geq u$ for all~$u\in(0,1)$.
 
 For~$\mathbf{z}\in(0,1)^{k-k^0}\times(x,1)$, the conditional density of~$G|\{\overline \imath_1,\ldots,\overline \imath_K,F_{K+1}, G^{[k,k^0]}=\mathbf{z}\}$ is
 \begin{align}
 \mathrm{(const)}\,\mathds 1_{g\in(0,1)^K}&\mathds 1_{g^{[k,k^0]}=\mathbf{z}}
 \prod_{m< k^0}g_m^{K-m}\cosh\big[{\mu^0_{\overline\imath_m}}((1-F_{K+1})\prod_{\ell=1}^mg_\ell+F_{K+1})\big]\notag]\\
 &\times \prod_{k^0\leq m\leq k}\mathbf{z}_m^{K-m}\cosh\big[{\mu^0_{\overline\imath_m}}((1-F_{K+1})\prod_{1\leq \ell<k^0}\!\!g_\ell\,\,\prod_{n=k^0}^m\mathbf{z}_n+F_{K+1})\big]\notag\\
&\times \prod_{k<m}g_m^{K-m}\cosh\big[{\mu^0_{\overline\imath_m}}((1-F_{K+1})\prod_{1\leq \ell<k^0}\!\!g_\ell\,\,\prod_{n=k^0}^k\mathbf{z}_n\prod_{k< \ell\leq m}\!\!g_\ell+F_{K+1})\big]\,.\notag
 \end{align}
Set~$\tau:=\prod_{n=k^0}^kz'_n/\prod_{n=k^0}^kz_n\geq 1$ and~$G'_{k}=\tau G_{k^0+1}$ so that 
 \[
\Big[\prod_{n=k^0}^kz'_n\Big] G_{k+1}=\Big[\prod_{n=k^0}^kz_n\Big] G'_{k+1}\,.
 \]
Then the proof follows the same idea as in {\it Step 3.2} and we will not detail it here.
 \medskip
 
 \noindent
 {$\circ$ \it Step 3.4: } This is the last step of the proof. Assume that we have built~$z':=(z'_{K},\ldots,z'_{k^0})$ and~$z:=(z_{K},\ldots,z_{k^0})$. Denote~$\mu_{z}^{(k^0-1)}$ the following conditional law  
 \[
 \mu_{z}^{(k^0-1)}:=\mathrm{law}\big[G_{k^0-1}|\{\overline \imath_1,\ldots,\overline \imath_K,F_{K+1}, G^{[K,k^0]}=z\}\big]\,,
 \]
 and~$\mathds{F}_{z}^{(k^0-1)}$ its cdf. Denote~$\mu_{z'}^{(k^0-1)}$ the following conditional law  
 \[
 \mu_{z'}^{(k^0-1)}:=\mathrm{law}\big[G_{k^0-1}|\{\overline \imath_1,\ldots,\overline \imath_K,F_{K+1}, G^{[K,k^0]}=z'\}\big]\,,
 \]
 and~$\mathds{F}_{z'}^{(k^01)}$ its cdf. Note that~$z\leq z'=T^{(K)}(z)\leq 1$. Again, we would prove that~$\mathds{F}_{z}^{(k^0-1)}\geq \mathds{F}_{z'}^{(k^0-1)}$ which implies that the transport map~$T^{(k^0-1)}:=\big(\mathds{F}_{z'}^{(k^0-1)}\big)^{-1}\circ \mathds{F}_{z}^{(k^0-1)}$ satisfies~$T^{(k^0-1)}(u)\geq u$ for all~$u\in(0,1)$.

For~$\mathbf{z}\in(0,1)^{K-k^0}\times(x,1)$, the conditional density of~$G|\{\overline \imath_1,\ldots,\overline \imath_K,F_{K+1}, G^{[K,k^0]}=\mathbf{z}\}$ is
 \begin{align}
 \mathrm{(const)}\,\mathds 1_{g\in(0,1)^K}&\mathds 1_{g^{[K,k^0]}=\mathbf{z}}
 \prod_{m< k^0}g_m^{K-m}\cosh\big[{\mu^0_{\overline\imath_m}}((1-F_{K+1})\prod_{\ell=1}^mg_\ell+F_{K+1})\big]\notag\\
 &\times \prod_{k^0\leq m\leq K}\mathbf{z}_m^{K-m}\cosh\big[{\mu^0_{\overline\imath_m}}((1-F_{K+1})\prod_{1\leq \ell<k^0}\!\!g_\ell\,\,\prod_{n=k^0}^m\mathbf{z}_n+F_{K+1})\big]\,.\notag
 \end{align}

\noindent
Now, let~$(g_1,\ldots,g_{k^0-2})\in(0,1)^{k^0-2}$ be fixed and denote by
 \begin{align}
\forall g\in(0,1),\quad
w_{z}(g):=&g^{K-k^0+1}\cosh\big[{\mu^0_{\overline\imath_{k^0-1}}}((1-F_{K+1})\prod_{\ell=1}^{k^0-2}g_\ell\times g+F_{K+1})\big]\notag\\
 &\times \prod_{k^0\leq m\leq K}\mathbf{z}_m^{K-m}\cosh\big[{\mu^0_{\overline\imath_m}}((1-F_{K+1})\prod_{n=k^0}^m\mathbf{z}_n\prod_{\ell=1}^{k^0-2}g_\ell\times g+F_{K+1})\big]\,.\notag
 \end{align}
 and, substituting~$z$ by~$z'$, define~$w_{z'}$ as well. Let~$t\in(0,1)$. Following the idea of  {\it Step 3.2}, one can check that it is sufficient to prove that
 \[
 \int_0^t\Big(\int_0^1w_{z}(g)w_{z'}(g')\mathrm dg'\Big)\mathrm dg
 \geq
  \int_0^1\Big(\int_0^tw_{z}(g)w_{z'}(g')\mathrm dg'\Big)\mathrm dg\,.
 \]
 Substituting 
 \[
  \int_0^t\Big(\int_0^tw_{z}(g)w_{z'}(g')\mathrm dg'\Big)\mathrm dg
 \]
 on both parts, one is reduced to prove that
  \[
 \int_0^t\Big(\int_t^1w_{z}(g)w_{z'}(g')\mathrm dg'\Big)\mathrm dg
 \geq
\int_0^t\Big(\int_t^1w_{z'}(g)w_{z}(g')\mathrm dg'\Big)\mathrm dg\,.
 \]
 Observe that~$g\leq g'$ in the last two integrals. Now, we have this lemma whose proof is omitted. 
 \begin{lemma} Let~$0<a\leq a'$ and~$b>0$. The function 
\[
z\mapsto\frac{\cosh(a\, z+b)}{\cosh(a'z+b)}
\]
is non-increasing on the domain~$(0,\infty)$.
\end{lemma}

\noindent
Let~$g\leq g'$. From Lemma~\ref{lem:coshyoyo2}, we deduce that~$\cosh(a g+b)\cosh(a' g'+b)\geq \cosh(a g'+b)\cosh(a' g+b)$, proving that~$w_{z}(g)w_{z'}(g')\geq w_{z'}(g)w_{z}(g')$. It proves that~$T^{(k^0-1)}(u)\geq u$ for all~$u\in(0,1)$.

We then proceed by induction for~$k^0-1\to k^0-2\to\cdots\to 1$. The proof follows the same line as above, {\it Step 3.4}.

nodes.name: Knothe-Rosenblatt map
nodes.statement_short: Define the Knothe-Rosenblatt map in a chosen order.

nodes.name: Step 3.1
nodes.statement_short: First coordinate map is nondecreasing.
nodes.statement:
{$\circ$ \it Step 3.1: } We start by the first transport map~$T^{(k^0)}:[0,1]\mapsto[0,1]$. Denote~$\mu_x^{(k^0)}$ the following conditional law  
 \[
 \mu_x^{(k^0)}:=\mathrm{law}\big[G_{k^0}|\{\overline \imath_1,\ldots,\overline \imath_K,F_{K+1},G_{k^0}\geq x\}\big]\,,
 \]
 and~$\mathds{F}_x^{(k^0)}$ its cdf. Note that the Knothe-Rosenblatt construction gives~$T^{(k^0)}=(\mathds{F}_y^{(k^0)})^{-1}\circ\mathds{F}_x^{(k^0)}$. We would like to prove that~$T^{(k^0)}(t)\geq t$ for all~$z\in(0,1)$. This is equivalent to prove that it holds~$ \mathds{F}_x^{(k^0)}\geq \mathds{F}_y^{(k^0)}$. For~$t\leq y$,~$\mathds{F}_y^{(k^0)}(t)=0$ and it implies that~$ \mathds{F}_x^{(k^0)}(t)\geq \mathds{F}_y^{(k^0)}(t)$. Let~$t>y$, using the conditional density~$\mathbf{p}$ defined in~\eqref{eq:density}, note that
 
 \begin{align*}
 \mathds{F}_x^{(k^0)}(t)\geq \mathds{F}_y^{(k^0)}(t)\quad&\Leftrightarrow\quad 
 \frac  {\int_x^t\mathbf{p}}  {\int_x^1\mathbf{p}}    \geq 
 \frac  {\int_y^t\mathbf{p}}  {\int_y^1\mathbf{p}} \\
 &\Leftrightarrow\quad \int_x^t \int_y^1 \mathbf{p}\otimes\mathbf{p}
 
 \geq \int_y^t   \int_x^1\mathbf{p}\otimes\mathbf{p},
 \end{align*}
where, for example
\[
\int_x^t \mbox{ means the integral over the  hyper rectangle }  [x,t]
:=\Big\{(g_1,\ldots,g_K)\in[0,1]^K\ :\!\ x\leq g_{k^0}\leq t\Big\}.
\]
A simple calculation (see also Figure~\ref{fig:yoyo}) gives that
\[
\int_x^t \int_y^1 \mathbf{p}\otimes\mathbf{p} = \int_y^t   \int_x^1\mathbf{p}\otimes\mathbf{p} +
\int_{[x,y] \times [t,1]}
\mathbf{p}\otimes\mathbf{p}\,,
\]
and it proves that~$ \mathds{F}_x^{(k^0)}\geq \mathds{F}_y^{(k^0)}$.

nodes.name: Step 3.2
nodes.statement_short: Second coordinate map is nondecreasing via a cosh inequality.
nodes.statement:
{$\circ$ \it Step 3.2: } We continue with the second transport map in Knothe-Rosenblatt construction. Let~$z_{k^0}\in(x,1)$ and denote~$\mu_{z_{k^0}}^{(k^0+1)}$ the following conditional law  
 \[
 \mu_{z_{k^0}}^{(k^0+1)}:=\mathrm{law}\big[G_{k^0+1}|\{\overline \imath_1,\ldots,\overline \imath_K,F_{K+1}, G_{k^0}=z_{k^0}\}\big]\,,
 \]
 and~$\mathds{F}_{z_{k^0}}^{(k^0+1)}$ its cdf. Let~$z'_{k^0}:=T^{(k^0)}(z'_{k^0})$ and denote~$\mu_{z'_{k^0}}^{(k^0+1)}$ the following conditional law  
 \[
 \mu_{z'_{k^0}}^{(k^0+1)}:=\mathrm{law}\big[G_{k^0+1}|\{\overline \imath_1,\ldots,\overline \imath_K,F_{K+1}, G_{k^0}=z'_{k^0}\}\big]\,,
 \]
 and~$\mathds{F}_{z'_{k^0}}^{(k^0+1)}$ its cdf. Note that~$x<z_{k^0}\leq z'_{k^0}=T^{(k^0)}(z_{k^0})\leq 1$. Again, we would like to prove that~$\mathds{F}_{z_{k^0}}^{(k^0+1)}\geq \mathds{F}_{z'_{k^0}}^{(k^0+1)}$ which implies that the transport map~$T^{(k^0+1)}:=\big(\mathds{F}_{z'_{k^0}}^{(k^0+1)}\big)^{-1}\circ \mathds{F}_{z_{k^0}}^{(k^0+1)}$ satisfies~$T^{(k^0+1)}(u)\geq u$ for all~$u\in(0,1)$.
 
 Recall that the conditional density~$\mathbf{p}$ of~$G|\{\overline \imath_1,\ldots,\overline \imath_K,F_{K+1}\}$ is given by~\eqref{eq:density} and recall that~$k^0\in I_0$. Observe that~$\mu^0_{k^0}=0$, so that the conditional density of~$G|\{\overline \imath_1,\ldots,\overline \imath_K,F_{K+1}, G_{k^0}=\mathbf{z}\}$ is
 \begin{align}
 \mathrm{(const)}\,\mathds 1_{g\in(0,1)^K}\mathds 1_{g_{k^0}=\mathbf{z}}&\prod_{k< k^0}g_k^{K-k}\cosh\big[{\mu^0_{\overline\imath_k}}((1-F_{K+1})\prod_{\ell=1}^kg_\ell+F_{K+1})\big] \\&\times \prod_{k> k^0}g_k^{K-k}\cosh\big[{\mu^0_{\overline\imath_k}}((1-F_{K+1})\,\,\mathbf{z}\!\!\prod_{1\leq \ell\neq k^0\leq k}\!\!g_\ell+F_{K+1})\big]\,.\notag
 \end{align}
 Set~$\tau:=z'_{k^0}/z_{k^0}\geq 1$ and~$G'_{k^0+1}=\tau G_{k^0+1}$ so that 
 \[
 z_{k^0} G_{k^0+1}=z'_{k^0}G'_{k^0+1}\,.
 \]
 Denote~$G':=(G_1,\ldots,G_{k^0-1},G'_{k^0+1},G_{k^0+2},\ldots,G_K)\in(0,1)^{k^0-1}\times(0,\tau)\times(0,1)^{K-k^0-1}$ and note that the conditional density of~$G'|\{\overline \imath_1,\ldots,\overline \imath_K,F_{K+1}, G_{k^0}=\tau \mathbf{z}\}$ is
 \begin{align*}
 \mathrm{(const)}\,\mathds 1_{g\in(0,1)^{k^0-1}\times(0,\tau)\times(0,1)^{K-k^0-1}}
 &\prod_{k< k^0}g_k^{K-k}\cosh\big[{\mu^0_{\overline\imath_k}}((1-F_{K+1})\prod_{\ell=1}^kg_\ell+F_{K+1})\big]
 \\&\times \prod_{k> k^0}g_k^{K-k}\cosh\big[{\mu^0_{\overline\imath_k}}((1-F_{K+1})\,\,\mathbf{z}\!\!\prod_{1\leq \ell\neq k^0\leq k}\!\!g_\ell+F_{K+1})\big]\,,
 \end{align*}
 which, up to some normalising constant, is the same as~\eqref{yoyoz1} up to the following change of support
 \[
 \mathds 1_{g\in(0,1)^K}\leftrightarrow \mathds 1_{g'\in(0,1)^{k^0-1}\times(0,\tau)\times(0,1)^{K-k^0-1}}\,.
 \]
 By an abuse of notation, we denote by~$\mathbf{p}$ this function, namely
 \begin{align*}
\mathbf{p}(g)=
 &\prod_{k< k^0}g_k^{K-k}\cosh\big[{\mu^0_{\overline\imath_k}}((1-F_{K+1})\prod_{\ell=1}^kg_\ell+F_{K+1})\big]
 \\&\times \prod_{k> k^0}g_k^{K-k}\cosh\big[{\mu^0_{\overline\imath_k}}((1-F_{K+1})\,\,\mathbf{z}\!\!\prod_{1\leq \ell\neq k^0\leq k}\!\!g_\ell+F_{K+1})\big]\,.
 \end{align*}
We deduce that
\begin{align}
 \mathds{F}_{z_{k^0}}^{(k^0+1)}(t)\geq \mathds{F}_{z'_{k^0}}^{(k^0+1)}(t)\quad
 &\Leftrightarrow\quad \overline{\mathds{P}}(G_{k^0+1}\leq t|G_{k^0}=z_{k^0})\geq
 \overline{\mathds{P}}(G_{k^0+1}\leq t|G_{k^0}=z'_{k^0})\notag\\
 &\Leftrightarrow\quad \overline{\mathds{P}}(G_{k^0+1}\leq t|G_{k^0}=z_{k^0})\geq
 \overline{\mathds{P}}(G'_{k^0+1}\leq \tau t|G_{k^0}=\tau z_{k^0})\notag\\
 &\Leftrightarrow\quad \frac{\int_{\mathcal{D}(t)}\mathbf{p}}{\int_{\mathcal{D}(1)}\mathbf{p}} \geq \frac{\int_{\mathcal{D}(\tau t)}\mathbf{p}}{\int_{\mathcal{D}(\tau)}\mathbf{p}}\notag\\
&\Leftrightarrow\quad \int_{\mathcal{D}(t)\times\mathcal{D}(\tau) }\mathbf{p}\otimes\mathbf{p}\geq\int_{\mathcal{D}(\tau t)\times \mathcal{D}(1)}\mathbf{p}\otimes\mathbf{p}\,, \end{align}
where
\[
 \mathcal{D}(s):=\Big\{(g_1,\ldots,g_{k^0-1},g_{k^0+1}\ldots,g_K)\in(0,1)^{K-1}\ :\ 0< g_{k^0+1}\leq s\Big\}\,.
\]
\begin{figure}
\includegraphics[width=0.4\textwidth]{y2}
\caption{The two boxed rectangles have Lebesgue measure, namely~$\tau t$. The~$\mathbf{p}\otimes\mathbf{p}$  measure of the grey box is greater than the~$\mathbf{p}\otimes\mathbf{p}$ measure of the white box. } \end{figure}

We now present an inequality on the  to conclude. Observe that we are integrating on domains depicted in Figure~\ref{fig:yoyo2}. The two boxes have same area for the uniform measure and we would like to compare their respective measure for the~$\mathbf{p}\otimes\mathbf{p}$ measure. We start by the next lemma whose proof is omitted. 
\begin{lemma} Let~$a,b\geq0$. The function 
\[
z\mapsto\cosh(a\, z+b)\times \cosh(a / z+b)
\]
is non-decreasing on the domain~$[1,\infty)$.
\end{lemma}

\noindent
Now, let~$(g_1,\ldots,g_{k^0-1},g_{k^0+2}\ldots,g_K)\in(0,1)^{K-1}$ be fixed in the integrals~\eqref{eq:yoyo123}. We are the looking at the weights of the domains~$(h_1,h_2)\in(0,t)\times (0,\tau)$ and~$(h_3,h_4)\in(0,\tau t)\times (0,1)$ for the weight function~$w$ given by
\begin{align*}
w(h_1,h_2)=&\mathrm{C}_1h_1^{K-k^0-1}\cosh\big[{\mu^0_{\overline\imath_k}}((1-F_{K+1})\,\,z_{k^0}\!\!\prod_{1\leq \ell <k^0}\!\!g_\ell\times h_1+F_{K+1})\big]\\
&\times \prod_{k> k^0+1}\cosh\big[{\mu^0_{\overline\imath_k}}((1-F_{K+1})\,\,z_{k^0}\!\!\prod_{1\leq \ell\neq k^0,k^0+1\leq k}\!\!g_\ell\times h_1+F_{K+1})\big]\\
&\times h_2^{K-k^0-1}\cosh\big[{\mu^0_{\overline\imath_k}}((1-F_{K+1})\,\,z_{k^0}\!\!\prod_{1\leq \ell <k^0}\!\!g_\ell\times h_2+F_{K+1})\big]\\
&\times \prod_{k> k^0+1}\cosh\big[{\mu^0_{\overline\imath_k}}((1-F_{K+1})\,\,z_{k^0}\!\!\prod_{1\leq \ell\neq k^0,k^0+1\leq k}\!\!g_\ell\times h_2+F_{K+1})\big]\,,
 \end{align*}
 where the constant~$\mathrm{C}_1$ depends on~$(g_1,\ldots,g_{k^0-1},g_{k^0+2}\ldots,g_K)\in(0,1)^{K-1}$. By the change of variables~$h'_1=h_3/t$ and~$h'_2=t h_4$, the right hand term of~\eqref{eq:yoyo123} is given by the integration on the domain~$(h'_1,h'_2)\in(0,t)\times (0,\tau)$ of the weight function~$w'$ given by
\begin{align*}
w'(h_1',h_2')=
 &\mathrm{C}_1{h'_1}^{K-k^0-1}\cosh\big[{\mu^0_{\overline\imath_k}}((1-F_{K+1})\,\,z_{k^0}\!\!\prod_{1\leq \ell <k^0}\!\!g_\ell\times t\times h'_1+F_{K+1})\big]\\
&\times \prod_{k> k^0+1}\cosh\big[{\mu^0_{\overline\imath_k}}((1-F_{K+1})\,\,z_{k^0}\!\!\prod_{1\leq \ell\neq k^0,k^0+1\leq k}\!\!g_\ell\times t\times h'_1+F_{K+1})\big]\\
 &\times {h'_2}^{K-k^0-1}\cosh\big[{\mu^0_{\overline\imath_k}}((1-F_{K+1})\,\,z_{k^0}\!\!\prod_{1\leq \ell <k^0}\!\!g_\ell\times h'_2/t+F_{K+1})\big]\\
&\times \prod_{k> k^0+1}\cosh\big[{\mu^0_{\overline\imath_k}}((1-F_{K+1})\,\,z_{k^0}\!\!\prod_{1\leq \ell\neq k^0,k^0+1\leq k}\!\!g_\ell\times h'_2/t+F_{K+1})\big]\,.
 \end{align*}
Now, invoke Lemma~\ref{lem:coshyoyo} with 
\begin{align*}
a&={\mu^0_{\overline\imath_k}}(1-F_{K+1})\,\,z_{k^0}\!\!\prod_{1\leq \ell <k^0}\!\!g_\ell\times  h\\
b&={\mu^0_{\overline\imath_k}}F_{K+1}\\
z&=t\geq 1\,,
\end{align*}
where~$h=h_1$ or~$h_2$, to get that~$w'\geq w$ and so 
\[
\int_{\mathcal{D}(t)\times\mathcal{D}(\tau) }\mathbf{p}\otimes\mathbf{p}\geq\int_{\mathcal{D}(\tau t)\times \mathcal{D}(1)}\mathbf{p}\otimes\mathbf{p}\,,
\]
which concludes this part of the proof.

nodes.statement_short: Rescale $G_{k^0+1}$ and reduce to a product-measure inequality.
nodes.statement:
Recall that the conditional density~$\mathbf{p}$ of~$G|\{\overline \imath_1,\ldots,\overline \imath_K,F_{K+1}\}$ is given by~\eqref{eq:density} and recall that~$k^0\in I_0$.  \end{align}
 Set~$\tau:=z'_{k^0}/z_{k^0}\geq 1$ and~$G'_{k^0+1}=\tau G_{k^0+1}$ so that 
 \[
 z_{k^0} G_{k^0+1}=z'_{k^0}G'_{k^0+1}\,.
 \]
 Denote~$G':=(G_1,\ldots,G_{k^0-1},G'_{k^0+1},G_{k^0+2},\ldots,G_K)\in(0,1)^{k^0-1}\times(0,\tau)\times(0,1)^{K-k^0-1}$ and note that the conditional density of~$G'|\{\overline \imath_1,\ldots,\overline \imath_K,F_{K+1}, G_{k^0}=\tau \mathbf{z}\}$ is
 \begin{align*}
 \mathrm{(const)}\,\mathds 1_{g\in(0,1)^{k^0-1}\times(0,\tau)\times(0,1)^{K-k^0-1}}
 &\prod_{k< k^0}g_k^{K-k}\cosh\big[{\mu^0_{\overline\imath_k}}((1-F_{K+1})\prod_{\ell=1}^kg_\ell+F_{K+1})\big]
 \\&\times \prod_{k> k^0}g_k^{K-k}\cosh\big[{\mu^0_{\overline\imath_k}}((1-F_{K+1})\,\,\mathbf{z}\!\!\prod_{1\leq \ell\neq k^0\leq k}\!\!g_\ell+F_{K+1})\big]\,,
 \end{align*}
 which, up to some normalising constant, is the same as~\eqref{yoyoz1} up to the following change of support
 \[
 \mathds 1_{g\in(0,1)^K}\leftrightarrow \mathds 1_{g'\in(0,1)^{k^0-1}\times(0,\tau)\times(0,1)^{K-k^0-1}}\,.
 \]
 By an abuse of notation, we denote by~$\mathbf{p}$ this function, namely
 \begin{align*}
\mathbf{p}(g)=
 &\prod_{k< k^0}g_k^{K-k}\cosh\big[{\mu^0_{\overline\imath_k}}((1-F_{K+1})\prod_{\ell=1}^kg_\ell+F_{K+1})\big]
 \\&\times \prod_{k> k^0}g_k^{K-k}\cosh\big[{\mu^0_{\overline\imath_k}}((1-F_{K+1})\,\,\mathbf{z}\!\!\prod_{1\leq \ell\neq k^0\leq k}\!\!g_\ell+F_{K+1})\big]\,.
 \end{align*}
We deduce that
\begin{align}
 \mathds{F}_{z_{k^0}}^{(k^0+1)}(t)\geq \mathds{F}_{z'_{k^0}}^{(k^0+1)}(t)\quad
 &\Leftrightarrow\quad \overline{\mathds{P}}(G_{k^0+1}\leq t|G_{k^0}=z_{k^0})\geq
 \overline{\mathds{P}}(G_{k^0+1}\leq t|G_{k^0}=z'_{k^0})\notag\\
 &\Leftrightarrow\quad \overline{\mathds{P}}(G_{k^0+1}\leq t|G_{k^0}=z_{k^0})\geq
 \overline{\mathds{P}}(G'_{k^0+1}\leq \tau t|G_{k^0}=\tau z_{k^0})\notag\\
 &\Leftrightarrow\quad \frac{\int_{\mathcal{D}(t)}\mathbf{p}}{\int_{\mathcal{D}(1)}\mathbf{p}} \geq \frac{\int_{\mathcal{D}(\tau t)}\mathbf{p}}{\int_{\mathcal{D}(\tau)}\mathbf{p}}\notag\\
&\Leftrightarrow\quad \int_{\mathcal{D}(t)\times\mathcal{D}(\tau) }\mathbf{p}\otimes\mathbf{p}\geq\int_{\mathcal{D}(\tau t)\times \mathcal{D}(1)}\mathbf{p}\otimes\mathbf{p}\,, \end{align}
where
\[
 \mathcal{D}(s):=\Big\{(g_1,\ldots,g_{k^0-1},g_{k^0+1}\ldots,g_K)\in(0,1)^{K-1}\ :\ 0< g_{k^0+1}\leq s\Big\}\,.
\]

&\times \prod_{k> k^0+1}\cosh\big[{\mu^0_{\overline\imath_k}}((1-F_{K+1})\,\,z_{k^0}\!\!\prod_{1\leq \ell\neq k^0,k^0+1\leq k}\!\!g_\ell\times h'_2/t+F_{K+1})\big]\,.

a&={\mu^0_{\overline\imath_k}}(1-F_{K+1})\,\,z_{k^0}\!\!\prod_{1\leq \ell <k^0}\!\!g_\ell\times  h\\

nodes.name: Step 3.3
nodes.statement_short: Induction for later coordinates, as in Step 3.2.
nodes.statement:
{$\circ$ \it Step 3.3: } We continue by induction with the other transport maps in Knothe-Rosenblatt's construction. Assume that we have built~$z':=(z'_{k},\ldots,z'_{k^0})$ and~$z:=(z_{k},\ldots,z_{k^0})$ for some~$k>k^0$. Denote~$\mu_{z}^{(k+1)}$ the following conditional law  
 \[
 \mu_{z}^{(k+1)}:=\mathrm{law}\big[G_{k+1}|\{\overline \imath_1,\ldots,\overline \imath_K,F_{K+1}, \underbrace{G_{k}=z_{k},\ldots, G_{k^0}=z_{k^0}}_{\mathrm{denoted\ }G^{[k,k^0]}=z}\}\big]\,,
 \]
 and~$\mathds{F}_{z}^{(k+1)}$ its cdf. Denote~$\mu_{z'}^{(k+1)}$ the following conditional law  
 \[
 \mu_{z'}^{(k+1)}:=\mathrm{law}\big[G_{k+1}|\{\overline \imath_1,\ldots,\overline \imath_K,F_{K+1}, \underbrace{G_{k}=z'_{k},\ldots, G_{k^0}=z'_{k^0}}_{G^{[k,k^0]}=z'}\}\big]\,,
 \]
 and~$\mathds{F}_{z'}^{(k+1)}$ its cdf. Note that~$z\leq z'=T^{(k)}(z)\leq 1$. Again, we would prove that~$\mathds{F}_{z}^{(k+1)}\geq \mathds{F}_{z'}^{(k+1)}$ which implies that the transport map~$T^{(k+1)}:=\big(\mathds{F}_{z'}^{(k+1)}\big)^{-1}\circ \mathds{F}_{z}^{(k+1)}$ satisfies~$T^{(k+1)}(u)\geq u$ for all~$u\in(0,1)$.
 
 For~$\mathbf{z}\in(0,1)^{k-k^0}\times(x,1)$, the conditional density of~$G|\{\overline \imath_1,\ldots,\overline \imath_K,F_{K+1}, G^{[k,k^0]}=\mathbf{z}\}$ is
 \begin{align}
 \mathrm{(const)}\,\mathds 1_{g\in(0,1)^K}&\mathds 1_{g^{[k,k^0]}=\mathbf{z}}
 \prod_{m< k^0}g_m^{K-m}\cosh\big[{\mu^0_{\overline\imath_m}}((1-F_{K+1})\prod_{\ell=1}^mg_\ell+F_{K+1})\big]\notag]\\
 &\times \prod_{k^0\leq m\leq k}\mathbf{z}_m^{K-m}\cosh\big[{\mu^0_{\overline\imath_m}}((1-F_{K+1})\prod_{1\leq \ell<k^0}\!\!g_\ell\,\,\prod_{n=k^0}^m\mathbf{z}_n+F_{K+1})\big]\notag\\
&\times \prod_{k<m}g_m^{K-m}\cosh\big[{\mu^0_{\overline\imath_m}}((1-F_{K+1})\prod_{1\leq \ell<k^0}\!\!g_\ell\,\,\prod_{n=k^0}^k\mathbf{z}_n\prod_{k< \ell\leq m}\!\!g_\ell+F_{K+1})\big]\,.\notag
 \end{align}
Set~$\tau:=\prod_{n=k^0}^kz'_n/\prod_{n=k^0}^kz_n\geq 1$ and~$G'_{k}=\tau G_{k^0+1}$ so that 
 \[
\Big[\prod_{n=k^0}^kz'_n\Big] G_{k+1}=\Big[\prod_{n=k^0}^kz_n\Big] G'_{k+1}\,.
 \]
Then the proof follows the same idea as in {\it Step 3.2} and we will not detail it here.

nodes.name: Step 3.4
nodes.statement_short: Earlier coordinates via a ratio-of-cosh lemma; induction downwards.
nodes.statement:
{$\circ$ \it Step 3.4: } This is the last step of the proof. Assume that we have built~$z':=(z'_{K},\ldots,z'_{k^0})$ and~$z:=(z_{K},\ldots,z_{k^0})$. Denote~$\mu_{z}^{(k^0-1)}$ the following conditional law  
 \[
 \mu_{z}^{(k^0-1)}:=\mathrm{law}\big[G_{k^0-1}|\{\overline \imath_1,\ldots,\overline \imath_K,F_{K+1}, G^{[K,k^0]}=z\}\big]\,,
 \]
 and~$\mathds{F}_{z}^{(k^0-1)}$ its cdf. Denote~$\mu_{z'}^{(k^0-1)}$ the following conditional law  
 \[
 \mu_{z'}^{(k^0-1)}:=\mathrm{law}\big[G_{k^0-1}|\{\overline \imath_1,\ldots,\overline \imath_K,F_{K+1}, G^{[K,k^0]}=z'\}\big]\,,
 \]
 and~$\mathds{F}_{z'}^{(k^01)}$ its cdf. Note that~$z\leq z'=T^{(K)}(z)\leq 1$. Again, we would prove that~$\mathds{F}_{z}^{(k^0-1)}\geq \mathds{F}_{z'}^{(k^0-1)}$ which implies that the transport map~$T^{(k^0-1)}:=\big(\mathds{F}_{z'}^{(k^0-1)}\big)^{-1}\circ \mathds{F}_{z}^{(k^0-1)}$ satisfies~$T^{(k^0-1)}(u)\geq u$ for all~$u\in(0,1)$.

For~$\mathbf{z}\in(0,1)^{K-k^0}\times(x,1)$, the conditional density of~$G|\{\overline \imath_1,\ldots,\overline \imath_K,F_{K+1}, G^{[K,k^0]}=\mathbf{z}\}$ is
 \begin{align}
 \mathrm{(const)}\,\mathds 1_{g\in(0,1)^K}&\mathds 1_{g^{[K,k^0]}=\mathbf{z}}
 \prod_{m< k^0}g_m^{K-m}\cosh\big[{\mu^0_{\overline\imath_m}}((1-F_{K+1})\prod_{\ell=1}^mg_\ell+F_{K+1})\big]\notag\\
 &\times \prod_{k^0\leq m\leq K}\mathbf{z}_m^{K-m}\cosh\big[{\mu^0_{\overline\imath_m}}((1-F_{K+1})\prod_{1\leq \ell<k^0}\!\!g_\ell\,\,\prod_{n=k^0}^m\mathbf{z}_n+F_{K+1})\big]\,.\notag
 \end{align}

\noindent
Now, let~$(g_1,\ldots,g_{k^0-2})\in(0,1)^{k^0-2}$ be fixed and denote by
 \begin{align}
\forall g\in(0,1),\quad
w_{z}(g):=&g^{K-k^0+1}\cosh\big[{\mu^0_{\overline\imath_{k^0-1}}}((1-F_{K+1})\prod_{\ell=1}^{k^0-2}g_\ell\times g+F_{K+1})\big]\notag\\
 &\times \prod_{k^0\leq m\leq K}\mathbf{z}_m^{K-m}\cosh\big[{\mu^0_{\overline\imath_m}}((1-F_{K+1})\prod_{n=k^0}^m\mathbf{z}_n\prod_{\ell=1}^{k^0-2}g_\ell\times g+F_{K+1})\big]\,.\notag
 \end{align}
 and, substituting~$z$ by~$z'$, define~$w_{z'}$ as well. Let~$t\in(0,1)$. Following the idea of  {\it Step 3.2}, one can check that it is sufficient to prove that
 \[
 \int_0^t\Big(\int_0^1w_{z}(g)w_{z'}(g')\mathrm dg'\Big)\mathrm dg
 \geq
  \int_0^1\Big(\int_0^tw_{z}(g)w_{z'}(g')\mathrm dg'\Big)\mathrm dg\,.
 \]
 Substituting 
 \[
  \int_0^t\Big(\int_0^tw_{z}(g)w_{z'}(g')\mathrm dg'\Big)\mathrm dg
 \]
 on both parts, one is reduced to prove that
  \[
 \int_0^t\Big(\int_t^1w_{z}(g)w_{z'}(g')\mathrm dg'\Big)\mathrm dg
 \geq
\int_0^t\Big(\int_t^1w_{z'}(g)w_{z}(g')\mathrm dg'\Big)\mathrm dg\,.
 \]
 Observe that~$g\leq g'$ in the last two integrals. Now, we have this lemma whose proof is omitted. 
 \begin{lemma} Let~$0<a\leq a'$ and~$b>0$. The function 
\[
z\mapsto\frac{\cosh(a\, z+b)}{\cosh(a'z+b)}
\]
is non-increasing on the domain~$(0,\infty)$.
\end{lemma}

\noindent
Let~$g\leq g'$. From Lemma~\ref{lem:coshyoyo2}, we deduce that~$\cosh(a g+b)\cosh(a' g'+b)\geq \cosh(a g'+b)\cosh(a' g+b)$, proving that~$w_{z}(g)w_{z'}(g')\geq w_{z'}(g)w_{z}(g')$. It proves that~$T^{(k^0-1)}(u)\geq u$ for all~$u\in(0,1)$.

We then proceed by induction for~$k^0-1\to k^0-2\to\cdots\to 1$. The proof follows the same line as above, {\it Step 3.4}.

nodes.name: Goal
nodes.statement_short: Goal for coordinate $k^0-1$.
nodes.statement:
This is the last step of the proof. Assume that we have built~$z':=(z'_{K},\ldots,z'_{k^0})$ and~$z:=(z_{K},\ldots,z_{k^0})$. Denote~$\mu_{z}^{(k^0-1)}$ the following conditional law  
 \[
 \mu_{z}^{(k^0-1)}:=\mathrm{law}\big[G_{k^0-1}|\{\overline \imath_1,\ldots,\overline \imath_K,F_{K+1}, G^{[K,k^0]}=z\}\big]\,,
 \]
 and~$\mathds{F}_{z}^{(k^0-1)}$ its cdf. Denote~$\mu_{z'}^{(k^0-1)}$ the following conditional law

 \mu_{z'}^{(k^0-1)}:=\mathrm{law}\big[G_{k^0-1}|\{\overline \imath_1,\ldots,\overline \imath_K,F_{K+1}, G^{[K,k^0]}=z'\}\big]\,,
 \]

Again, we would prove that~$\mathds{F}_{z}^{(k^0-1)}\geq \mathds{F}_{z'}^{(k^0-1)}$ which implies that the transport map~$T^{(k^0-1)}:=\big(\mathds{F}_{z'}^{(k^0-1)}\big)^{-1}\circ \mathds{F}_{z}^{(k^0-1)}$ satisfies~$T^{(k^0-1)}(u)\geq u$ for all~$u\in(0,1)$.

nodes.name: Reduction
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to an inequality on weights $w_z$, $w_{z'}$.
nodes.statement:
For~$\mathbf{z}\in(0,1)^{K-k^0}\times(x,1)$, the conditional density of~$G|\{\overline \imath_1,\ldots,\overline \imath_K,F_{K+1}, G^{[K,k^0]}=\mathbf{z}\}$ is
 \begin{align}
 \mathrm{(const)}\,\mathds 1_{g\in(0,1)^K}&\mathds 1_{g^{[K,k^0]}=\mathbf{z}}

 &\times \prod_{k^0\leq m\leq K}\mathbf{z}_m^{K-m}\cosh\big[{\mu^0_{\overline\imath_m}}((1-F_{K+1})\prod_{1\leq \ell<k^0}\!\!g_\ell\,\,\prod_{n=k^0}^m\mathbf{z}_n+F_{K+1})\big]\,.\notag
 \end{align}

\noindent
Now, let~$(g_1,\ldots,g_{k^0-2})\in(0,1)^{k^0-2}$ be fixed and denote by
 \begin{align}
\forall g\in(0,1),\quad
w_{z}(g):=&g^{K-k^0+1}\cosh\big[{\mu^0_{\overline\imath_{k^0-1}}}((1-F_{K+1})\prod_{\ell=1}^{k^0-2}g_\ell\times g+F_{K+1})\big]\notag\\
 &\times \prod_{k^0\leq m\leq K}\mathbf{z}_m^{K-m}\cosh\big[{\mu^0_{\overline\imath_m}}((1-F_{K+1})\prod_{n=k^0}^m\mathbf{z}_n\prod_{\ell=1}^{k^0-2}g_\ell\times g+F_{K+1})\big]\,.\notag
 \end{align}
 and, substituting~$z$ by~$z'$, define~$w_{z'}$ as well. Let~$t\in(0,1)$. Following the idea of  {\it Step 3.2}, one can check that it is sufficient to prove that
 \[
 \int_0^t\Big(\int_0^1w_{z}(g)w_{z'}(g')\mathrm dg'\Big)\mathrm dg
 \geq
  \int_0^1\Big(\int_0^tw_{z}(g)w_{z'}(g')\mathrm dg'\Big)\mathrm dg\,.
 \]
 Substituting 
 \[
  \int_0^t\Big(\int_0^tw_{z}(g)w_{z'}(g')\mathrm dg'\Big)\mathrm dg
 \]
 on both parts, one is reduced to prove that
  \[
 \int_0^t\Big(\int_t^1w_{z}(g)w_{z'}(g')\mathrm dg'\Big)\mathrm dg
 \geq
\int_0^t\Big(\int_t^1w_{z'}(g)w_{z}(g')\mathrm dg'\Big)\mathrm dg\,.
 \]
 Observe that~$g\leq g'$ in the last two integrals.

nodes.name: Lemma block
nodes.statement_short: State the ratio-of-cosh lemma.
nodes.statement:
Now, we have this lemma whose proof is omitted. 
 \begin{lemma} Let~$0<a\leq a'$ and~$b>0$. The function 
\[
z\mapsto\frac{\cosh(a\, z+b)}{\cosh(a'z+b)}
\]
is non-increasing on the domain~$(0,\infty)$.
\end{lemma}

nodes.name: Monotonicity of a ratio of cosh
assumptions: Let~$0<a\leq a'$ and~$b>0$.
conclusions: is non-increasing on the domain~$(0,\infty)$

Let~$0<a\leq a'$ and~$b>0$. The function

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement_short: Apply the lemma and proceed by downward induction.
nodes.statement:
Let~$g\leq g'$. From Lemma~\ref{lem:coshyoyo2}, we deduce that~$\cosh(a g+b)\cosh(a' g'+b)\geq \cosh(a g'+b)\cosh(a' g+b)$, proving that~$w_{z}(g)w_{z'}(g')\geq w_{z'}(g)w_{z}(g')$. It proves that~$T^{(k^0-1)}(u)\geq u$ for all~$u\in(0,1)$.

We then proceed by induction for~$k^0-1\to k^0-2\to\cdots\to 1$. The proof follows the same line as above, {\it Step 3.4}.

nodes.name: Numerical integration on the hypercube
nodes.statement_short: Approximate $\int_{[0,1]^d}f$ by an average over $n$ points.
nodes.statement:
Our goal is to  compute  the integral of some function$f$  on  the  hypercube of dimension~$d$, namely
\[
I:= \int_{[0,1]^d}  f(x) dx.
\]
We want to approximate it by a finite sum over~$n$ points 
 \[
I_n:=  \frac 1 n \sum_{i=1}^n f(x^{(i)}).
\]
nodes.section: 8 A Quasi Monte Carlo (QMC) method: Cubature by lattice rule

nodes.name: Lattice rule
nodes.statement:
A convenient way of constructing the sequence~$x^{(i)}, i=1,\dots,n$ is the so-called {\it lattice rule}: from the first point~$x^{(1)}$ we deduce the others~$x^{(i)}$ by
 \[
x^{(i)} =  \big\{ i . x^{(1)}\big\},
\] 
where  the~$\{\}$ brackets mean that we take the fractional part coordinate by coordinate.
nodes.section: 8 A Quasi Monte Carlo (QMC) method: Cubature by lattice rule

nodes.name: Fast-rank algorithm
nodes.statement_short: Component-by-component construction of the lattice generator minimizing worst-case error in a Korobov RKHS.
nodes.statement:
The Fast-rank algorithm~\citep{NC}   is a fast algorithm that finds, component  by component and  as a function of the prime~$n$, the sequence of coordinates of~$x^{(1)}$ that minimizes the maximal error when~$f~$ varies in a unit ball~$\mathcal E$ of some {\it RKHS}, namely a tensorial product of {\it Koborov spaces}. In addition it gives an expression  of its minimax error, namely 
\[
 \max_{f\in \mathcal E}(f,n,x^{(1)}).
\]
nodes.section: 8 A Quasi Monte Carlo (QMC) method: Cubature by lattice rule

nodes.name: Randomized lattice rule with a Monte-Carlo layer
nodes.statement_short: Randomly shift the lattice by one uniform $U$, average $f$ over the shifted points, and repeat $N$ times to get confidence intervals.
nodes.statement:
A reliable estimate of the error is obtained by adding a {\it Monte-Carlo layer} as in~\cite{genz} for instance. This can be done as follows. Let~$U$ a {\bf unique} uniform variable on~$[0,1]^d$, we define
  \[
x^{(i)}_U:=  \big\{ i. x^{(1)} +U\big\}, \quad I_{n,U}:= \frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n f(x^{(i)}_U).
\] 
Classical computations show that~$I_{n,U}$ is now an unbiased estimator of~$I$.  In a final step,  we perform~$N$ (in practice 15-20) independent  repetitions of the experiment  above an we compute usual asymptotic confidence intervals for independent observations.
nodes.section: 8 A Quasi Monte Carlo (QMC) method: Cubature by lattice rule

nodes.name: Shifted lattice estimate
nodes.statement_short: Shift the lattice by a uniform $U$ and average.
nodes.statement:
Let~$U$ a {\bf unique} uniform variable on~$[0,1]^d$, we define
  \[
x^{(i)}_U:=  \big\{ i. x^{(1)} +U\big\}, \quad I_{n,U}:= \frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n f(x^{(i)}_U).
\]

nodes.name: Repetitions and CI
nodes.statement_short: Repeat $N$ times independently and compute confidence intervals.
nodes.statement: In a final step,  we perform~$N$ (in practice 15-20) independent  repetitions of the experiment  above an we compute usual asymptotic confidence intervals for independent observations.
